title: VanEck seeks to withdraw application for Lido staked Ether ETF
summary: VanEck initially filed an S-1 registration statement for the exchange-traded fund in October last year.
content:
VanEck initially filed an S-1 registration statement for the exchange-traded fund in October last year.

Asset manager VanEck said it no longer plans to proceed with its proposed Lido staked Ether exchange-traded fund, shelving the product designed to give investors exposure to the liquid staking token.

In an SEC filing on Wednesday, VanEck Digital Assets said it “does not intend to proceed with the planned distribution” of the trust’s shares. It did not explain what prompted the decision or whether VanEck would pursue a replacement product.

VanEck initially filed the fund’s S-1 registration statement on Oct. 16, 2025. The proposed fund would have held Lido staked Ether (stETH) and would expect to accrue certain staking rewards through ownership of stETH.

Cointelegraph reached out to VanEck Digital Assets for comment.

title: 21shares Strategist Sees Bitcoin Path to $90K After Hotter CPI Report
summary: Bitcoin could advance toward $90,000 once near-term economic uncertainty clears, according to 21shares strategist Matt Mena. He points to last week’s selling and historically positive returns after hotter core inflation prints as support for his outlook. Bitcoin’s $90K Forecast Faces an $85K Test Bi...
content:
Bitcoin could advance toward $90,000 once near-term economic uncertainty clears, according to 21shares strategist Matt Mena. He points to last week’s selling and historically positive returns after hotter core inflation prints as support for his outlook.

Key Takeaways

  • Mena identifies $85,000 as resistance before a potential $90,000 advance.
  • His analysis finds a 1.21% average weekly gain after hotter core CPI prints.
  • The strategist targets $2,800-$3,000 for ether and $130 for solana.

Bitcoin’s $90K Forecast Faces an $85K Test

Bitcoin could regain $85,000 and move toward $90,000 after upcoming economic releases, Matt Mena, senior crypto research strategist at crypto investment product issuer 21shares, told Bitcoin.com News in commentary supplied Oct. 14. He argued that last week’s decline below $85,000 had already reflected much of the downside risk associated with a hotter inflation reading.

“With PPI due tomorrow, the final major near-term macro data release will be out of the way ahead of this week’s FOMC meeting. That could set the stage for another test of $85k resistance,” Mena said, adding:

“While a pullback toward $81k remains possible, we believe the balance of risks favors a move through $85k and toward $90k once the remaining macro uncertainty clears.”

The Federal Reserve’s next Federal Open Market Committee meeting is scheduled for Oct. 27-28. The producer price index, or PPI, measures prices received by domestic producers and is due Oct. 15. Its designation as the final major near-term release reflects Mena’s assessment.

Hotter CPI Challenges Bitcoin’s Recovery

September’s consumer price index results showed prices rose 0.6% from August and 3.7% over the preceding year. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, increased 0.3% monthly and 2.6% annually. The monthly core reading exceeded the 0.2% economists had expected. Bitcoin subsequently fell below $83,000, toward $82,800, after the release.

Mena’s initial commentary described BTC as holding above $83,000 after previously testing the $81,000-$82,000 zone. Before the release, the retreat had also brought support near $81,300 into focus. His argument rests on that earlier selling having absorbed much of the inflation risk, even as subsequent trading tested the initial assessment.

The strategist views bitcoin, a decentralized digital currency, as a barometer of liquidity and investors’ willingness to hold riskier assets. His analysis puts BTC’s average return at 1.21% in the seven days following hotter-than-expected core CPI releases since 2023, supporting his interpretation that an inflation surprise need not prevent a recovery.

ETF Flows Frame Ether and Solana Price Targets

Institutional positioning provides another reference point, with bitcoin having twice rebounded near the $81,500 ETF cost basis identified by Glassnode. That benchmark estimates the acquisition price associated with U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded fund holdings. The analysis identified approximately $77,500 as the next major downside level if that support fails.

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs attracted $175.62 million in net inflows on Oct. 13, reversing the preceding session’s withdrawals. Fidelity’s spot bitcoin ETF, FBTC, received $103.06 million, while Blackrock’s equivalent fund, IBIT, brought in $65.89 million. Ether funds also returned to positive flows, drawing $24.84 million after 10 consecutive sessions of net redemptions.

Mena also cited quarterly ETF inflows exceeding $3 billion for ETH and $500 million for SOL, describing their strongest quarter this year. He expects ether to consolidate around $2,500 in the near term before another attempt at $2,800-$3,000. For solana, the strategist identified $130 as a potential price level by the end of the quarter.

title: Polygon gains US payments licenses after closing Coinme deal
summary: The deal gives Polygon access to 37 money transmitter licenses and 11 state exemptions.
content:
Polygon Labs has completed its acquisition of Coinme, giving its stablecoin payments platform a regulated way to convert dollars into digital assets and back across 48 US states.

Polygon said Wednesday its US payments business now has coverage with 37 money transmitter licenses and 11 exemptions. It is also registered with the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FINCEN) as a money services business.

The acquisition follows agreements announced in January to buy Coinme and wallet infrastructure provider Sequence for more than $250 million combined, while consolidating some roles at Polygon Labs. At the time, Polygon CEO Marc Boiron said it needed the team to transition into a “leading payments-focused blockchain company.”

Coinme is a licensed crypto exchange and cash-to-cryptocurrency platform that lets users buy and sell digital assets through cash, debit cards and bank transfers. When the acquisition was first announced, Coinme had more than one million users and a retail network spanning 50,000 locations, according to Polygon.

Open Money Stack gives businesses “a more direct route between stablecoins and local currency,” said Rahul Shinghal, co-founder and CEO of cross-border payments company Tazapay, one of the platform’s first customers.

Related: Polygon CEO announces job cuts amid Coinme acquisition

title: Evernorth Rings Nasdaq Closing Bell, Showcasing XRP Treasury
summary: Evernorth’s 473 million XRP treasury took the spotlight at Nasdaq’s closing bell. The ceremony highlighted a corporate investment model that connects stock ownership with actively managed cryptocurrency holdings. Nasdaq Ceremony Highlights Publicly Traded XRP Exposure Stock investors’ access to an a...
content:
Evernorth’s 473 million XRP treasury took the spotlight at Nasdaq’s closing bell. The ceremony highlighted a corporate investment model that connects stock ownership with actively managed cryptocurrency holdings.

Key Takeaways

  • Asheesh Birla led the Oct. 14 ceremony at Nasdaq MarketSite.
  • Evernorth raised about $300 million in gross cash proceeds at closing.
  • Deployment with Ripple, Kraken, Coinbase, and Bitgo is planned for Q4.

Nasdaq Ceremony Highlights Publicly Traded XRP Exposure

Stock investors’ access to an actively managed XRP treasury took the spotlight as Evernorth Holdings Inc. (Nasdaq: XRPN) rang the Nasdaq closing bell Oct. 14. Founder and CEO Asheesh Birla led the ceremony at Nasdaq MarketSite in New York’s Times Square, celebrating the digital asset treasury company’s debut as a public company.

Nasdaq Exchange highlighted Evernorth’s role in providing investors with XRP exposure through a publicly listed structure in an Oct. 14 post on X. Investors buying XRPN acquire shares in the company, with exposure shaped by its holdings, investment decisions, financing, and operating performance.

The celebration followed Evernorth’s completed business combination with Armada Acquisition Corp. II on Oct. 9. At closing, Evernorth held approximately 473 million XRP and had raised about $300 million in gross cash proceeds before transaction expenses. Armada was a special purpose acquisition company formed to take another business public.

Active Management Targets Growth in XRP Per Share

The merger combined cash financing and XRP contributions from institutional and digital asset investors, including Arrington Capital, SBI Group, Ripple, Pantera Capital, Kraken, and GSR. Armada’s shareholder vote approving the proposed merger on Sept. 30 preceded the Oct. 9 closing.

Management’s active XRP treasury strategy seeks to increase XRP holdings per share through institutional investment strategies, decentralized finance, ecosystem participation, and capital markets activities. XRP per share measures token holdings relative to outstanding stock, making changes in the share count relevant alongside growth in the treasury’s total assets.

Investment oversight rests with Chief Investment Officer Hugo Jeandesboz, a former Coinbase Asset Management co-chief investment officer who reports to Birla. His responsibilities span allocation, liquidity management, active treasury management, and relationships with trading counterparties and custodians.

Evernorth Names Ripple, Kraken, Coinbase, and Bitgo as Deployment Partners

The ceremony coincided with Evernorth’s Oct. 14 announcement of Ripple, Kraken, Coinbase, and Bitgo as institutional execution partners. The company plans to accumulate XRP and deploy treasury assets into institutional strategies beginning in the fourth quarter. Its initial phase will use established counterparties under the oversight of Evernorth’s investment and risk team.

Expansion into decentralized finance would involve financial activity conducted through blockchain-based systems, including lending and trading applications. Evernorth intends to allocate capital directly to XRP Ledger markets as native lending and credit capabilities are activated by validators and demonstrated in production. That phase remains dependent on the network’s financial infrastructure maturing.

The company selected its initial partners based on institutional infrastructure, licensing, capitalization, and experience serving public companies and asset managers. Evernorth noted that partnership agreements remain subject to customary closing conditions and required regulatory and corporate approvals.

title: Brooklyn DA and FBI Crush Massive International Crypto Scam
summary: On Wednesday, Brooklyn prosecutors disclosed that they have dealt a major blow to an international cryptocurrency scam that stole tens of millions of dollars from Russian-speaking Americans, including many residents of the New York borough. Brooklyn Prosecutors and FBI Dismantle 241 Scam Websites an...
content:
On Wednesday, Brooklyn prosecutors disclosed that they have dealt a major blow to an international cryptocurrency scam that stole tens of millions of dollars from Russian-speaking Americans, including many residents of the New York borough.

Key Takeaways

  • Brooklyn prosecutors and the FBI dismantled 241 scam websites and 112 servers tied to an international crypto fraud operation.
  • The scheme stole tens of millions of dollars from Russian-speaking Americans, including Brooklyn residents.
  • Criminals targeted victims a second time with bogus recovery services promising to retrieve stolen cryptocurrency.

Brooklyn Prosecutors and FBI Dismantle 241 Scam Websites and 112 Servers

According to the Brooklyn District Attorney’s Virtual Currency Unit (VCU), the agency shut down around 241 fraudulent websites and 112 servers. The VCU further noted that the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) helped with the investigation. In the press release issued by the Brooklyn DA, prosecutors described the operation as one of the largest cyber enforcement actions ever carried out by a local prosecutor’s office.

“When scammers halfway around the world target Brooklyn residents, they should know they are not beyond our reach,” remarked Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez, in a statement. “These criminals stole many millions of dollars from Russian-speaking victims through an elaborate investment scheme, then tried to exploit them again with false promises to recover their money.”

Gonzalez credited the office’s VCU with exposing the fraud, tracing the stolen cryptocurrency, and uncovering the technological infrastructure sustaining the operation before joining forces with the FBI to dismantle it. “By disrupting more than 100 servers and hundreds of fraudulent websites, we have struck at the heart of this criminal enterprise and made it far harder for these scammers to victimize others,” Gonzalez added.

A Second Scam Targeted Victims Desperate to Recover Stolen Crypto

The latest news follows the Brooklyn DA’s digital currency case from last year involving a man who stole nearly $16 million from roughly 100 victims by impersonating crypto exchange support staff. He pleaded guilty and was recently sentenced to up to 12 years in prison. In the cryptocurrency scam complaint revealed on Wednesday, investigators discovered another troubling part of the operation.

Weeks after stealing someone’s cryptocurrency, the scammers would contact the victim again, this time claiming they could help recover the stolen funds. This is called a recovery scam, in which criminals exploit people who have already lost money by offering false promises of getting it back. In other words, the criminals weren’t satisfied with stealing the initial investment. They also attempted to take advantage of victims’ desperation to recover their savings.

“This case is a prime example of what can be done through the power of our partnerships with state, local, and international law enforcement,” explained James C. Barnacle, assistant director in charge of the FBI’s New York field office. “Our partners at Kings County District Attorney’s Office were swift to involve our subject matter experts and together we got to the bottom of the plot, seizing over one hundred domains.”

TMGM has been named the Official Financial Online Trading Sponsor of BIGBANG 2026–2027 WORLD TOUR <XX : COSMOS> in Sydney, bringing together the Sydney-founded global broker and one of Asia’s most recognised music acts as BIGBANG celebrates its 20th anniversary.

Taking place at Accor Stadium on 31 October 2026, the Sydney concert forms part of BIGBANG’s first world tour since 2017. The tour marks two decades since the group’s debut and its return to major international stages across Asia, North America, Europe and Oceania.

The partnership marks an expansion of TMGM’s international sponsorship strategy into live entertainment. Since its founding in Sydney in 2013, TMGM has used international partnerships to build brand recognition beyond financial markets, with sport forming a significant part of its sponsorship portfolio.

Working with BIGBANG brings a new cultural dimension to that strategy. Over two decades, the South Korean group has built an international following extending across music, fashion and popular culture, creating an opportunity for TMGM to connect with audiences through one of the most established names in K-pop.

“BIGBANG has built a remarkable legacy over the past 20 years, with an influence that reaches well beyond music,” said TMGM. “There is also something particularly meaningful about bringing this partnership to Sydney, where TMGM began. As we continue to grow internationally, we want our partnerships to reflect the audiences and markets we engage with around the world.”

title: Two Polymarket Whales Face Off in $500K Seahawks-Broncos Showdown
summary: Polymarket whales are setting up a titanic clash for Thursday night’s game between the Denver Broncos and the Seattle Seahawks. The top earner of the week, with $2.13 million in profit, has bet about $214,000 on the Broncos to win, while a trader down more than $700,000 this week put $290,000 on Sea...
content:
Polymarket whales are setting up a titanic clash for Thursday night’s game between the Denver Broncos and the Seattle Seahawks. The top earner of the week, with $2.13 million in profit, has bet about $214,000 on the Broncos to win, while a trader down more than $700,000 this week put $290,000 on Seattle.

Key Takeaways

  • BreakTheBank bought 500,528 Broncos shares at 42 cents, matched against surfandturf’s Seahawks orders.
  • surfandturf paid $290,000 for 500,000 Seahawks shares at 58 cents in the same transaction on Oct. 13.

Massive Sums Moved for Single Game

At 22:34 UTC on Oct. 13, a single Polymarket transaction paired two of the platform’s biggest sports traders on opposite sides of Thursday Night Football. An account trading as BreakTheBank bought 500,528 Broncos shares at 42 cents, spending $213,879. Its order was filled by six resting limit orders from surfandturf on Polymarket’s public order book, which bought 500,000 Seahawks shares at 58 cents for $290,000.

Polymarket shares are binary contracts that pay $1 if the outcome happens and nothing if it does not, so the trade created a pot of about $500,000 that goes to whichever side wins. If Denver wins, then BreakTheBank, which has since added a few hundred shares and holds 500,812, would clear about $287,000. If Seattle wins, then surfandturf, which has sold about 7,100 shares at around 57 cents and held about 492,900 on Wednesday, would clear about $207,000.

Each account is now by far the largest holder on its side of the moneyline market, where about 537,000 shares have traded in total. The market had Seattle at 57% on Wednesday. The game kicks off at 8:15 p.m. ET on Thursday, Oct. 15, in Denver. Single-game positions this size can swing late: On Oct. 11, another account lost a $147,000 Eagles bet to a 57-yard field goal as time expired.

BreakTheBank, created in January, sits first on Polymarket’s weekly and monthly profit leaderboards, at $2.13 million and $3.57 million, and is up $7.04 million all-time. This week it netted about $913,000 on the Buffalo Bills’ 37-34 overtime win over the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night, and $458,182 on Barcelona’s 4-1 win at Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday.

The account called surfandturf was created in April and is up about $67,000 all-time after losing about $718,000 this week. It lost $413,671 backing the Atlanta Falcons, who fell 30-23 to the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday night, and $61,000 on the Rams in the game BreakTheBank won. The two have been on opposite sides before: On Sept. 27, surfandturf lost $515,803 on the Rams against the Broncos, a game on which BreakTheBank made about $306,000 backing Denver.

In their most recent trades, surfandturf bought only one side of each market, which points to a directional bettor rather than a market maker—the latter being a user who posts orders to both buy and sell in a market and profits from the gap between those prices, whoever wins. A directional bettor picks a side and wins or loses with the result.

title: Russia’s Central Bank Authorizes Sberbank to Exchange Cryptocurrencies
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Russia’s Central Bank Authorizes Sberbank to Exchange Cryptocurrencies
Sberbank will debut its bitcoin-related products in December. 
This post Russia’s Central Bank Authorizes Sberbank to Exchange Cryptocurrencies first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di Salv...
content:
Russia’s central bank has added Sberbank to its register of organizations authorized to exchange digital currencies, according to reports. 

Sberbank was added to the list of digital depositories, which will keep a record of cryptocurrencies and digital rights, earlier this month. 

Now, it joins eight other organizations on the exchange register, including state-controlled VTB, Russia’s second-largest bank, and T-Invest Lab, part of T-Technologies, which also owns online lender T-Bank, according to a Monday report from Interfax. 

The announcement comes as Russia fast moves forward with Bitcoin-related regulation. Sberbank last month announced that it was the first in the country to have been approved to custody bitcoin. 

The Bank of Russia gave it the green light for “digital currency record-keeping” and to facilitate the transfer of such assets, covering bitcoin and other, smaller cryptocurrencies. 

“This status will allow the bank to provide services related to organizing the circulation of digital currency on interfaces which clients already use,” Sberbank was quoted saying in the news report. 

A law on digital currencies and digital rights came into effect in Russia on September 1, creating a comprehensive legal framework for cryptocurrency circulation. Transactions involving cryptocurrencies can be conducted via the existing infrastructure of exchanges, brokers and trustees, and now also via crypto exchanges and digital depositories. 

Cryptocurrency can be bought and sold via crypto exchanges, while the rights to these assets are recorded in digital depositories.

Banks and other organizations have been able to apply to the CBR for the corresponding licenses since October 5. Some existing players have simplified access to the market and can obtain licenses on a notification basis within just one day.

Under the new rules, unqualified investors will be able to buy bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies including stablecoins, within a limit of 300,000 rubles ($3,556) per year through one intermediary. 

Qualified investors will have access to all cryptocurrencies traded on the exchange and over-the-counter markets.

Sberbank will debut its crypto wallet in December — the same month the Moscow Exchange will debut crypto trading.

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Polygon Rolls Out US-Regulated Payments With Completed Coinme Deal
summary: Polygon Labs has completed its acquisition of crypto payments company Coinme, bringing regulated U.S. payment capabilities to its Open Money Stack platform and expanding its push into stablecoin-powered financial services. Polygon Gets Regulated Payments via Coinme Polygon Labs announced Wednesday, ...
content:
Polygon Labs has completed its acquisition of crypto payments company Coinme, bringing regulated U.S. payment capabilities to its Open Money Stack platform and expanding its push into stablecoin-powered financial services.

Key Takeaways

  • Polygon Labs completed its acquisition of Coinme, expanding its regulated payments coverage to 48 U.S. states.
  • Polygon’s Open Money Stack is a unified platform connecting stablecoins, banking services, and blockchain payments.
  • Tazapay, Mesh, Toku and Kira are early adopters, using the platform for cross-border payments, payroll, and financial services.

Polygon Gets Regulated Payments via Coinme

Polygon Labs announced Wednesday, Oct. 14, that it has finalized its acquisition of Coinme, giving its payments business regulatory coverage across 48 U.S. states through 37 state money transmitter licenses and 11 applicable exemptions. The business is also registered with the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) as a money services business.

The acquisition represents a significant step in Polygon’s strategy to connect blockchain-based payments with traditional financial infrastructure, allowing businesses to move money between banks, payment networks, and stablecoins through a unified platform.

Polygon’s Open Money Stack (OMS) combines digital wallets, payment routing, blockchain settlement, and banking integrations. The company says the platform allows businesses to manage the full lifecycle of a payment, from accepting fiat currency through bank transfers, cards, or cash deposits to settling transactions onchain and distributing funds in local currencies.

Rather than requiring businesses to maintain separate relationships with multiple infrastructure providers, Polygon—an Ethereum scaling network—aims to consolidate these functions through a single integration. The company also identified Tazapay, Mesh, Toku, and Kira as among the first businesses adopting the platform.

Tazapay, which serves more than 1,000 enterprises and fintech companies across over 30 countries, is integrating Polygon’s wallet and fiat conversion infrastructure to streamline cross-border transactions. Mesh, a crypto payments network connecting more than 300 wallets, exchanges and financial services, is adding Polygon’s fiat on-ramp capabilities to expand funding options for digital asset transactions.

Meanwhile, global payroll provider Toku is using Polygon’s wallet and payout infrastructure to help workers receive stablecoin payments and convert their earnings into local currencies. Kira, an AI-powered financial services platform, is integrating OMS to expand stablecoin access alongside U.S. banking services, including ACH, Fedwire, and Fednow payments.

The announcement underscores Polygon’s growing emphasis on payments infrastructure as blockchain companies seek to capture a larger share of traditional financial activity.

By combining Coinme’s regulated U.S. payments operations with existing blockchain technology, Polygon is positioning itself as an infrastructure provider for businesses looking to incorporate stablecoins without building their own banking and compliance integrations.

title: Organizations join forces to fight Illinois crypto tax, after 6-month pause
summary: Illinois officials already agreed to delay implementation of a 0.2% tax on crypto assets, but industry-aligned organizations are pushing for summary judgment on the merits.
content:
The Crypto Council for Innovation (CCI) and Blockchain Association (BA) said they would join the Digital Chamber and others to push for a court to address the merits of a lawsuit over Illinois’s digital-asset tax, set to take effect in 2027. 

In a Tuesday filing in the Circuit Court of Sangamon County, the crypto advocacy organizations asked the court to approve an expedited schedule for summary judgment “to reach a decision on the tax’s lawfulness as quickly as possible.” The filing cited the CCI’s and BA’s lawsuit against Illinois state officials, as well as one filed separately by the Digital Chamber and Illinois Blockchain Association.

“While pausing enforcement of the Digital Asset Tax Act protects Illinois consumers and businesses from this onerous and legally flawed tax until July 1, it remains imperative that the merits are determined as soon as possible,” said CCI CEO Ji Kim. 

Earlier this month, Illinois officials agreed to delay implementation of the 0.2% crypto tax law for six months, from Jan. 1 to July 1, 2027. The decision, part of the Digital Chamber’s lawsuit, came in response to claims that the digital asset tax had been “slipped into the state’s budget” without debate or public feedback. Digital Chamber CEO Cody Carbone said at the time that the organization would continue with legal proceedings “until this tax is struck down for good.”

Related: French lawmakers back stablecoin swap tax in 2027 budget bill

The expedited schedule, subject to court approval, could allow a decision on the merits of the law by March.

Leadership shakeup at Blockchain Association this week

On Friday, Summer Mersinger is scheduled to step down as CEO of the Blockchain Association as part of a leadership transition. Mersinger joined the advocacy group last year after resigning from the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission.

Kristin Smith, the organization’s former CEO, will step in as interim head, though Mersinger is expected to stay on until the end of 2026.

title: Perpetual Futures on US Stocks Could Go Live Within Weeks, SEC Official Says
summary:
At least four exchanges are expected to start trading perpetual futures on securities this quarter, the SEC’s top market-structure official said, signalling that a contract born in crypto markets is close to entering regulated US equity derivatives trading.
Speaking at the Security Traders Associati...
content:
2026-10-14T22:45:00.000+02:00

Wednesday, 14/10/2026 | 20:45 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Five CFTC-regulated exchanges filed SEC security futures registration notices in September.
  • The expected launches would follow CME’s introduction of cash-settled single-stock futures.

At least four exchanges are expected to start trading perpetual futures on securities this quarter, the SEC’s top market-structure official said, signalling that a contract born in crypto markets is close to entering regulated US equity derivatives trading.

Speaking at the Security Traders Association’s annual market structure conference on 14 October, Selway said: “I expect at least four to begin to trade perpetual futures on securities sometime this quarter.”

Five CFTC-Regulated Exchanges File With SEC

Five CFTC-regulated exchanges - Coinbase, Kalshi, Bitnomial, NADEX and ICE Futures - submitted Form 1-N registration notices in September, ahead of the anticipated launches.

All five were already designated contract markets, or DCMs, registered with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.

The process differs from a conventional exchange application requiring SEC approval. Under the applicable framework, an eligible exchange’s registration becomes effective when it submits the required notice.

The SEC’s rules expressly distinguish Form 1-N notices from applications the Commission would approve before trading begins. That registration has a limited purpose: trading security futures products.

It does not give the venues general authorisation to operate a cash-equities exchange, and it is separate from the timing and terms of individual contract launches.

Perpetual Contracts Would Extend Securities Futures Trading

The expected launches would follow CME’s introduction of cash-settled single-stock futures on 27 July, which Selway cited in his remarks.

CME’s launch announcement covered more than 50 US stocks, expanding listed derivatives tied to individual companies. However, unlike perpetual futures, those conventional contracts have expiry dates.

Selway described the SEC’s responsibility as ensuring compliance with regulatory standards and supporting competition to protect investors. Assessing whether new products would succeed commercially was outside that role.

“Our role is not to judge the likely commercial success or failure of these projects. Rather, we work to ensure compliance with our standards and to foster healthy competition, to best protect and benefit investors,” he said.

The five September filings establish the registration step, but the speech does not identify which four venues Selway expects to launch during Q4. It also leaves individual launch dates, eligible securities, leverage limits, funding arrangements and settlement terms unspecified.

title: Chainlink Expands Market Data to Stellar’s $4B Tokenized Asset Ecosystem
summary: Chainlink’s data infrastructure is now live on the Stellar blockchain, opening the door to new decentralized finance (DeFi) applications across a network that already supports more than $4 billion in tokenized real-world assets (RWAs). Chainlink Arrives on Stellar The Stellar Development Foundation ...
content:
Chainlink’s data infrastructure is now live on the Stellar blockchain, opening the door to new decentralized finance (DeFi) applications across a network that already supports more than $4 billion in tokenized real-world assets (RWAs).

Key Takeaways

  • Chainlink is now live on Stellar, providing market data infrastructure for DeFi applications.
  • The integration supports lending, trading, and tokenized assets across Stellar’s $4 billion RWA ecosystem.
  • Stellar aims to expand its DeFi capabilities, attracting developers, institutions, and liquidity.

Chainlink Arrives on Stellar

The Stellar Development Foundation announced that Chainlink’s Data Feeds and Data Streams are available to developers, providing market data to help fuel lending platforms, prediction markets, perpetual futures exchanges, and other blockchain-based financial services.

The integration represents a push to expand Stellar’s role beyond issuing and transferring tokenized assets, enabling those assets to be traded, used as collateral, and incorporated into more sophisticated financial products.

Chainlink’s oracle technology supplies external market information to blockchain apps, allowing smart contracts to access pricing data necessary for activities such as determining collateral values, calculating loan-to-value ratios, and triggering automated liquidations.

According to the foundation, Stellar ecosystem applications are already adopting the infrastructure to support lending operations and stablecoin pricing.

The launch follows Stellar’s earlier decision to join the Chainlink Scale program, under which the network committed funding to make Chainlink’s infrastructure more affordable for developers. The broader partnership also includes plans to integrate Chainlink’s Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol (CCIP), although that component was not included in the latest launch announcement.

“The Stellar network’s adoption of Chainlink as its data infrastructure unlocks a new generation of DeFi and tokenized asset applications across its ecosystem,” said Chainlink Labs Chief Business Officer Johann Eid, in a statement.

Raja Chakravorti, chief business officer at the Stellar Development Foundation, emphasized that issuing tokenized assets represents only the first stage of developing blockchain-based financial markets.

“Tokenization is only the beginning,” Chakravorti said, adding that institutional-scale markets require dependable systems for pricing, execution, and asset movement.

The integration comes as blockchain networks compete to attract financial institutions and developers seeking to bring traditional financial assets onchain. Stellar has established a presence in tokenized assets and payments, but expanding their usefulness within DeFi could help attract additional liquidity and applications.

For Stellar, the latest development is an effort to transform its growing inventory of tokenized assets into a more active financial ecosystem, where capital can be borrowed against, traded, and deployed across decentralized markets.

title: Standard Chartered Brings Bitcoin Trading and Custody to Affluent UAE Clients
summary: On Wednesday, the banking giant managing nearly $1 trillion in assets, Standard Chartered, revealed it is making new moves inroads in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The bank explained that it is making it possible for wealthy clients in the UAE to buy and sell bitcoin and ether directly through the...
content:
On Wednesday, the banking giant managing nearly $1 trillion in assets, Standard Chartered, revealed it is making new moves inroads in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The bank explained that it is making it possible for wealthy clients in the UAE to buy and sell bitcoin and ether directly through their regular bank accounts.

Key Takeaways

  • Standard Chartered now lets wealthy UAE clients trade bitcoin and ether directly through their bank accounts.
  • The bank partnered with Zodia Markets to offer crypto trading, custody, and settlement services.
  • Dubai’s VARA approved the service, which initially supports only bitcoin and ether for eligible clients.

Standard Chartered Brings Crypto Trading Directly to UAE Bank Accounts

Customers do not need to open an account at a centralized cryptocurrency exchange (CEX) or manage a separate digital wallet. The bank said on Wednesday that this is the first time it has offered such a service anywhere in the world. It also claims to be the first international bank to introduce this type of cryptocurrency trading service in the UAE.

“As client interest in digital assets continues to grow, this launch represents a significant milestone for Standard Chartered as we bring digital assets into our core wealth offering,” explained Samir Subberwal, Standard Chartered’s global head of wealth solutions, retail products, data, and analytics. “With digital assets moving into mainstream wealth conversations, clients are increasingly looking not only for access, but also for the security, trust, and confidence that comes from investing through a regulated and trusted institution.”

Subberwal added:

“As a leading international wealth manager, we remain focused on delivering innovative solutions that help clients capture investment opportunities in a rapidly evolving market.”

Zodia Markets Partnership Powers Bank’s New Crypto Offering

The bank will take responsibility for holding crypto assets and settling digital currency transfers. At the same time, Standard Chartered is working with Zodia Markets, a cryptocurrency trading company backed by its investment arm, SC Ventures. The partnership combines the bank’s customer services with professional cryptocurrency trading and storage systems.

The service has received approval from Dubai’s Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (VARA), the agency responsible for regulating cryptocurrency businesses in Dubai. “The UAE was a natural choice for this launch, given the country’s forward-looking approach to innovation, strong regulatory environment, and growing leadership in digital assets,” remarked Rola Abu Manneh, Standard Chartered’s CEO for the UAE, Middle East, and Pakistan.

For now, “eligible affluent clients” can buy and sell bitcoin (BTC) and ether (ETH), with the bank’s announcement making no mention of additional crypto assets.

title: SEC Clears Cboe KPI Options, with Robinhood Set for Retail Launch
summary:
The US Securities and Exchange Commission has approved Cboe’s proposal for listing binary options tied to corporate performance indicators. 
The platform submitted the proposed rule change to permit listing of binary options overlaying key performance indicators reported by selected stock issues in ...
content:
2026-10-14T21:17:07.164+02:00

Wednesday, 14/10/2026 | 19:17 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Binary KPI options on over 100 performance metrics will become available on Cboe in October 2026.
  • Both Cboe and Robinhood promised to waive fees on these contracts through year-end.

The US Securities and Exchange Commission has approved Cboe’s proposal for listing binary options tied to corporate performance indicators.

The platform submitted the proposed rule change to permit listing of binary options overlaying key performance indicators reported by selected stock issues in July 2026.

Once launched, the contracts would let investors trade on reported business metrics rather than on how a company’s share price reacts to them. Robinhood plans to be the first retail broker to offer the contracts.

Trading has not begun, and a separate application to clear the products remains pending.

Performance Metrics Become Tradable

The contracts will settle according to whether a company reports a particular key performance indicator above or below a predefined threshold.

The approved list contains over 100 metrics across 23 companies, including Apple’s iPhone revenue, Nvidia’s data-centre revenue, Tesla’s Model 3/Y production and Robinhood’s funded-customer count.

An investor could correctly forecast a company’s revenue but still lose money on a conventional stock option if the share price moved in the opposite direction for another reason. The new type of contracts give traders a more direct position on an earnings outcome.

Cboe’s products will be cash-settled, European-style options, meaning they can be exercised only at expiration. A successful contract will pay a fixed $1, while an unsuccessful one will expire without a payout.

Settlement will use the metric in the company’s relevant SEC filing, rather than an earlier earnings press release. Cboe can decide which contracts to list and set several thresholds around the most recently reported value.

A Securities-Market Route to Prediction Trading

The product takes a different regulatory route from event contracts offered through platforms such as Kalshi. Those markets operate on Commodity Futures Trading Commission-regulated exchanges, while Cboe’s KPI contracts will be securities listed on an SEC-regulated options exchange.

For retail brokers, that creates a way to offer prediction-style contracts under securities-options rules rather than through a separate prediction markets exchange.

Cboe and Robinhood had targeted an October launch, though the exact date has not been disclosed. Cboe plans to waive its exchange fees on the contracts through 2026, subject to regulatory review; Robinhood says it won't charge fees through year-end.

Before the trading starts, Cboe Clear U.S. needs to obtain temporary registration to clear the contracts.

Earlier this year the exchange launched Cboe Predicts, binary options on the Mini-S&P 500. The new contracts are listed under symbols XSPBW and XSPBX and allow traders take a "yes" or "no" position on whether XSP will close at or above a specified level.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, Standard Chartered pushed its $2 trillion stablecoin market forecast back to 2030, Kraken parent Payward agreed to acquire a Lithuanian bank as it expands into traditional financial services and Ledger suspended reseller sales across parts of Asia amid an investigation into tampered hardware wallets.

Standard Chartered delays $2 trillion stablecoin forecast to 2030

Standard Chartered has pushed back its forecast for when the stablecoin market will hit $2 trillion from 2028 to 2030, citing slower supply growth despite rising transaction activity.

The bank previously expected to reach the milestone by 2028, but stablecoin market capitalization has stayed near $309 billion this year. Geoffrey Kendrick, its head of digital assets research, said existing stablecoins are being used more frequently, even as the amount in circulation has leveled off.

Standard Chartered identified four major stablecoin markets. Tether’s USDT dominates savings in emerging economies, while Circle’s USDC leads payments in developed markets. USDC and Ethena’s USDe are prominent in crypto trading, with USDC also leading the smaller market for transactions between artificial intelligence agents.

Competition is expected to intensify in developed-market payments, where newer issuers and banking networks are challenging established providers. Kendrick said the distribution of interest earned on stablecoin reserves could influence which companies gain market share.

Meanwhile, proposed US accounting changes could treat qualifying stablecoins as cash equivalents on corporate balance sheets, potentially encouraging broader use in business payments and settlement.

Kraken parent to buy Lithuanian Saldo Bank amid TradFi expansion

Payward will buy Lithuania-based Saldo Bank as part of its expansion into traditional financial services, calling it “a deliberate next step in an infrastructure strategy we’ve been building for years.”

Payward signed a definitive agreement to acquire Saldo Finance Oy, a Finnish holding company whose subsidiary, Saldo Bank UAB, is a digital bank licensed in Lithuania, according to a Wednesday announcement.

Payward said Saldo Bank’s EU banking license and footprint will enable it to expand into four operating markets, including Lithuania, Finland, Sweden and Germany, where the bank already offers retail term deposits. The bank’s authorization is also passported into the Netherlands.

The acquisition is expected to close in 2027, subject to customary regulatory approvals. It would enable Payward Banking to offer traditional banking services, including interest on deposits, lending products and banking-as-a-service, such as card issuance, passporting and lending capabilities to small and medium enterprises.

Ledger asks resellers to halt sales in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong

Ledger has requested sellers and distributors of its devices in six Southeast Asian countries and Hong Kong to suspend sales and remove its hardware wallets from shelves as it investigates reports of tampered devices.

In a post on X on Tuesday, Ledger said the request covers resellers in Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia and Hong Kong.

“To be clear, as the investigation continues, the only confirmed incidents remain contained to Southeast Asia. We have not verified a drain linked to a device bought elsewhere,” said Ledger.

“The investigation is ongoing to determine who tampered with these devices and where in the distribution chain it happened,” it added.

The wider sales suspension request expands on Ledger’s earlier request for reseller CryptoBilis to stop sales and shipments. The investigation became public on Oct. 9 after reports of stolen crypto linked to devices purchased through the reseller.

title: EU authority classifies Circle’s USDC as ‘significant’ under MiCA
summary: The second-largest stablecoin by market cap will be overseen by French and EU authorities under its classification as a “significant e-money token.“
content:
The European Banking Authority (EBA) has classified Circle’s USDC stablecoin as a significant e-money token under the region’s Markets in Crypto Assets (MiCA) framework. 

In a Wednesday notice, the banking regulator said the e-money token classification, granted to only 45 other projects, effectively means the USDC stablecoin will be jointly overseen by the EBA and France’s supervisory authority, the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution. The stablecoin is the second largest by market capitalization, at $73 billion compared to Tether USDt’s $184 billion.

The “significant“ classification came as many EU-based token issuers pushed for regulated US dollar-pegged stablecoins in the region. Stable Mint CEO James Bennett told Cointelegraph that while Europe couldn’t “wish away“ dollar stablecoins, regulators could control safeguards and rules for issuers.

“For European corporates to make cross-border payments globally, offering only a euro stablecoin isn’t enough,” AllUnity CEO Alexander Höptner told Cointelegraph.

As authorities and issuers move closer to embracing dollar stablecoins, policymakers at the European Central Bank continue to explore the potential introduction of a digital euro. The EU authority first proposed the central bank digital currency in 2020, with the potential to issue the coin in 2029 after the conclusion of legislation and a pilot program.

title: OCC Blows Lid Off Debanking Practices at America’s 9 Bank Giants
summary: America’s largest national banks face fresh scrutiny after federal regulators discovered that all nine maintained policies that could restrict financial services based on political beliefs, religious affiliations, or lawful business activities. The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) rev...
content:
America’s largest national banks face fresh scrutiny after federal regulators discovered that all nine maintained policies that could restrict financial services based on political beliefs, religious affiliations, or lawful business activities. The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) reviewed nearly 100,000 complaints and 420,000 pages of documents, uncovering decisions involving Trump merchandise, conservative media companies, firearms businesses, and digital assets.

Key Takeaways

  • The OCC found all nine major banks maintained policies restricting access to financial services.
  • JPMorgan’s Wepay closed a Trump merchandise seller’s account in February 2021.
  • The OCC found banking restrictions affecting firearms, energy and digital asset businesses.

Selling Donald Trump merchandise, running a conservative media company, or operating a perfectly legal firearms business apparently carried an unexpected financial hazard: losing access to banking. On Wednesday, Oct. 14, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) took the wraps off an investigation into America’s nine largest national banks.

The OCC revealed that every institution maintained policies capable of restricting customers over political beliefs, religious affiliations, or lawful commercial activities. The findings cover the span from 2020 through September 2025 and draw on nearly 100,000 complaints and approximately 420,000 pages of internal documents. The regulator’s conclusion raises uncomfortable questions about who gets to hold a bank account.

Banking Giants Face Scrutiny Over Political and Religious Bias

In a comprehensive report, the OCC examined JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Citibank, Wells Fargo, U.S. Bank, Capital One, PNC, TD Bank, and BMO Bank. Its report found that broad reputation risk policies sometimes substituted subjective judgments for measurable financial concerns.

“The banks largely lacked clear and measurable standards and objective risk-based criteria for assessing the reputation risks of customers or prospective customers,” the report disclosed. Additionally, Comptroller Jonathan V. Gould came out swinging in the agency’s accompanying press release.

“Today’s report provides irrefutable evidence that the nation’s largest banks have denied, debanked and discriminated against customers and lawful businesses,” Gould declared. One particularly revealing example involved JPMorgan’s payment subsidiary, Wepay, which terminated an account selling merchandise supporting Trump and the Make America Great Again movement in February 2021.

An employee explained the decision internally. “We closed their account due to violating our Wepay’s Terms of Services (MAGA and Trump-related items are part of it),” the individual cited in the report states.

PNC’s Internal Emails Reveal Another Debanking Flashpoint

The American financial institution PNC declined to extend credit to a media company whose owners maintained prominent conservative political and religious associations. An internal employee questioned whether the bank should associate with the company at all.

“I think it becomes really difficult to justify aligning ourselves with a company whose owners have built very public personas around opinions very contrary to PNC’s beliefs/values,” the employee said. The investigation also identified an instance involving an organization whose political activities supported Democratic candidates, demonstrating that politically motivated restrictions were not confined to one party.

Beyond political affiliations, regulators found industry-specific restrictions affecting firearms manufacturers, coal companies, oil and gas businesses, detention facilities, tobacco companies, and digital asset activities.

The report put the consequences plainly:

“Policies adopting industry-specific restrictions had real-world consequences.”

Some banks imposed internal social standards on otherwise lawful firearms businesses, including restrictions involving magazine capacity and sales to customers younger than 21. Smaller businesses sometimes faced financing obstacles while established companies received exceptions.

Wealthy Clients Received Exceptions as Ordinary Customers Lost Access

The OCC report also uncovered a curious contradiction in how banks assessed reputation risk. Some customers lost access to services over unfavorable publicity or unverified allegations, while certain wealthy clients retained banking relationships despite attracting more serious negative attention.

The findings suggest reputation risk was not always applied consistently, particularly when valuable banking relationships were involved. The regulator also acknowledged that it could not establish the total number of affected customers or calculate the complete financial damage.

OCC Warns Banking Reforms Might Not Go Far Enough

Although banks have revised certain policies, regulators discovered that reputation risk considerations sometimes survived under alternative labels, including brand risk and franchise risk. Gould warned that voluntary changes might not be sufficient. “Notwithstanding certain efforts by the largest banks to rein in these practices, I am not confident that they will be enough,” he said.

The OCC has already eliminated reputation risk considerations from bank examinations and is weighing additional supervisory changes. “Fair access to financial services is not a mantra—it is a mandate,” Gould concluded.

For the nine banking giants, the heat is on. The more difficult question is whether eliminating controversial policies will also eliminate the discretion that allowed those policies to influence customer decisions in the first place.

title: Aptos Encrypted Mempool Goes Live, Shielding Trades From MEV Bots With 20ms Delay
summary:
Key Takeaways: Aptos started hiding details of pending transactions in its Encrypted Mempool on mainnet. Validators are not the first to process transactions, thereby mitigating the possibility of frontrunning and
The post Aptos Encrypted Mempool Goes Live, Shielding Trades From MEV Bots With 20ms D...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Aptos started hiding details of pending transactions in its Encrypted Mempool on mainnet.
  • Validators are not the first to process transactions, thereby mitigating the possibility of frontrunning and sandwich attacks.
  • The system brings in around 20 milliseconds of the delay per block for 50 nodes.

Aptos has activated a protocol-native encrypted mempool on mainnet, giving users an optional way to hide transaction details until block ordering is finalized. The feature aims at mitigating a longstanding issue in DeFi: frontrunning and sandwich attacks on visibly pending transactions via MEV tactics.

  • Aptos Encrypts Transactions Before They Enter the Mempool
  • No Single Validator Can Unlock a Pending Transaction
    • Encrypted Mempool Targets Frontrunning and Sandwich Bots
    • Aptos Adds Privacy With About 20ms of Extra Latency

Aptos Encrypts Transactions Before They Enter the Mempool

If the feature is enabled by the users, its transaction payload is encrypted on the client before being sent to the network. Sensitive information like function call and arguments are hidden, but the sender address and gas fee are still visible.

Validators then confirm the ordering of the transactions without having to view the payment message itself. Validators then collectively decrypt the transactions if consensus has agreed on the block, allowing them to execute the transactions and add them to the blockchain record.

Read More: Sui’s Hashi Launches With $500M to Turn Bitcoin Into Productive DeFi Collateral Markets

No Single Validator Can Unlock a Pending Transaction

Aptos implements threshold encryption directly based on its current set of validators. No single validator is able to decode a pending transaction nor is any of the group below its required stake threshold.

We do not create any additional decryption committee or any private block builder or trusted hardware provider in Aptos. Rather than that, AQUA token conversion is handled by the same validators that facilitate the Aptos consensus.

Encrypted Mempool Targets Frontrunning and Sandwich Bots

The public mempools show transaction data prior to execution. That’s where automated trading bots find some opportunity to spot huge transactions, copy or execute trades before and after another trader.

With the payload secret and confirmed repayment order solved, Aptos eliminates numerous of the information these bots need to disrupt holding trades.

Protection may be particularly relevant for institutional orders, big DeFi trades and automated agents, as early disclosure of transaction intention may result in execution risk.

Petra is first to make the feature available as part of its signing process, letting users choose to encrypt a transaction at sign time. Additionally, a perpetual futures exchange on Aptos, Decibel, will be using encrypted mempool infrastructure to ensure that orders remain off-chain until they are executed.

Read More: Robinhood Launches AI-Native Chain, Stock Tokens in 120+ Countries and 7% Crypto Yield

Aptos Adds Privacy With About 20ms of Extra Latency

Running threshold encryption at blockchain scale adds to the computation required, but according to Aptos, the performance effect is minimal.

Its batched encryption design will allow it to decrypt an entire block with constant-size communication per validator, regardless of the number of transactions in the batch.

Testing with 50 nodes resulted in an additional 20 milliseconds per block over the production version of AptosBFT. The delay is insignificant as Aptos blocks are finalized in less than a second.

Restrictions in both of the first implementations prevent complete transaction anonymity. Sender addresses and gas information are still visible, while the transaction payload itself remains encrypted until block finalization.

Existing Move smart contracts do not require changes, and support is available through the Aptos TypeScript SDK version 7.0.0 and later.

title: US authorities dismantle crypto scam network that stole tens of millions
summary: Brooklyn prosecutors and the FBI seized 112 servers and shut down 241 websites linked to investment scams that targeted Russian-speaking Americans.
content:
Prosecutors in Brooklyn, New York, working with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), have disrupted an Eastern European cryptocurrency scam network accused of stealing tens of millions of dollars from Americans, primarily Russian-speakers.

The operation, carried out last week and announced on Wednesday, resulted in the shutdown of 241 websites and the seizure of 112 servers hosted by companies in Eastern Europe and the United States, according to the Brooklyn District Attorney’s Office. No arrests were made.

“These criminals stole many millions of dollars from Russian-speaking victims through an elaborate investment scheme, then tried to exploit them again with false promises to recover their money,” Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez said in a statement. He credited the office’s Virtual Currency Unit and the FBI with uncovering the network’s infrastructure.

Seizing the servers was key to the operation because it disrupted the scammers’ ability to create new websites and contact victims. “We disabled the back end of the operation,” Assistant District Attorney Alona Katz, who led the investigation, said, according to Bloomberg.

The operation comes amid a rise in cryptocurrency-related fraud across the US. Americans reported $11.4 billion in crypto fraud losses in 2025, a 22% increase from the previous year, according to FBI figures cited by Bloomberg.

Related: Chinese crime network laundered over $1B for Lazarus: ZachXBT

title: Strategy Buys 250 Bitcoin for $21.5M, Sending Total Holdings to a Record 848,250 BTC
summary:
Key Takeaways: On its part, Strategy is said to have bought 250 BTC at $21.5 million or an average price of $86,194 per BTC. It owns a total of 848,250
The post Strategy Buys 250 Bitcoin for $21.5M, Sending Total Holdings to a Record 848,250 BTC appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • On its part, Strategy is said to have bought 250 BTC at $21.5 million or an average price of $86,194 per BTC.
  • It owns a total of 848,250 BTC, purchased at a total value of approximately $64.0 billion.
  • The company also used $192.4 million to buy back preferred STRC stock in the week.

Despite the purchase quantity decreasing, Strategy had added 250 Bitcoin to its holding between October 5 and October 11. Even as the buying volume subsided, Strategy had increased its Bitcoin holdings by 250 BTC between October 5 and 11.

The purchase brought the company’s total BTC holdings to 848,250 BTC, solidifying its position as the biggest corporate Bitcoin owners.

  • Strategy Adds 250 BTC for $21.5 Million
  • Bitcoin Treasury Reaches 848,250 BTC
    • Strategy Spends $192.4M Repurchasing STRC Shares
    • $4.88B Reserve Supports Strategy’s Bitcoin Capital Framework

Strategy Adds 250 BTC for $21.5 Million

In total, Strategy paid $21.5 million to buy the latest batch of Bitcoins including fees and expenses. The average price of acquiring one of these 250 BTC was $86,194 per Bitcoin for the company.

Income from two sources. Net proceeds from the sales of MSTR common stock funded an equal amount of the purchase; MSTR’s cash balance funded the remainder which amounted to approximately USD 500,000.

A total of 125,183 MSTR shares were sold this past week, yielding net proceeds of $21.0 million.

Bitcoin Treasury Reaches 848,250 BTC

As of 11 October, Strategy had 848,250 BTC in its balance. The total money allotted to the purchase of those assets at various times was around $64.0 billion, including fees and expenses, the company said.

That means Strategy has ended up paying an average of $75,444 per BTC for all of its Bitcoin holdings. The firm is sticking to its core capital approach, which involves equity issuance and cash reserves, and not on just one fund source, and continues to focus on the Bitcoin aspect of the business.

Strategy Spends $192.4M Repurchasing STRC Shares

Bitcoin was not the only big investment that Strategy made in the week. The Company purchased 1,932,145 STRC preferred shares for an aggregate purchase price of $192.4 million. STRF, STRK, STRD and MSTR have not had any repurchases reported for the same time period.

Strategy has $354.8 million under its optional preferred-stock repurchase program and $1.0 billion under its authorization to buy back MSTR common stock.

$4.88B Reserve Supports Strategy’s Bitcoin Capital Framework

As of October 11, Strategy also had $4.88 billion USD of Reserve and $640.5 million USD of separate USD Cash. The USD Reserve is the reserved share of the debt to support preferred-stock dividends and interest payments on the debt.

USD Cash can have a more salient role and may be used for the acquisition of Bitcoin, expansion of the reserves, or in other aspects of capital management. The firm has utilised $500,000 in those cash reservoirs for its latest Bitcoin investment, while the majority of the acquiring investment was made with new MSTR stock dollars.

title: BingX EU Secures Austrian MiCA Licence to Enter 29 EEA Markets
summary:
BingX EU, operated by
MEGE zweite GmbH, has secured a licence under the Markets in Crypto-Assets
Regulation from Austria’s Financial Market Authority. The authorisation is
expected to allow the company to offer regulated crypto services across the
European Economic Area, subject to applicable passpo...
content:
2026-10-14T19:39:05.128+02:00

Wednesday, 14/10/2026 | 17:39 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • The company has not announced a launch date or detailed its initial range of regulated crypto services.
  • The EU’s MiCA transition period ended on 1 July this year, requiring crypto firms to obtain authorisation.

BingX EU, operated by MEGE zweite GmbH, has secured a licence under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation from Austria’s Financial Market Authority. The authorisation is expected to allow the company to offer regulated crypto services across the European Economic Area, subject to applicable passporting requirements.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The licence comes as the EU’s transition to a common regulatory framework for crypto-asset service providers reaches its final stages. In June 2026, Finance Magnates examined how the end of the transition period would affect crypto firms operating in the region, including those that had not secured the required authorisation. National transition arrangements determine how existing providers move to the new framework.

BingX EU Licence Covers 29 EEA Countries

The licence covers 29 EEA countries, giving BingX EU a regulatory basis for expanding its services across the region. MiCA establishes common requirements for crypto-asset service providers, including rules on authorisation, business conduct and consumer protection.

Daniel Lai, Chief Executive Officer of BingX EU, said the company’s priority was to provide European users with a “trusted and locally regulated trading experience”.

“Operating under MiCA will allow us to deliver our services under a clear regulatory framework,” Lai said.

He said the framework would allow the company to serve European users while meeting regulatory requirements.

BingX EU is now MiCA-licensed in Europe. 🇪🇺 Read all the details. 👇

— BingX (@BingXOfficial) October 14, 2026

BingX EU Follows Bybit and KuCoin in Europe

BingX EU said it would continue working with the Austrian FMA and other European regulators as it prepares to launch its regulated services across the EEA. The company has not specified a launch date or provided details of the services it plans to offer initially through its regulated European entity.

Other crypto exchanges have also secured MiCA licences from Austria’s FMA. In May 2025, Bybit received authorisation to offer crypto services across 29 EEA countries through its Austrian operations. In November 2025, KuCoin EU Exchange GmbH also secured an Austrian MiCA licence covering 29 EEA markets, excluding Malta.

The post Standard Chartered Brings RLUSD Custody to XRPL in 3-Way Institutional Custody Program appeared fi...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • RLUSD’s listing on the XRP Ledger is now covered under Standard Chartered’s institutional custody program.
  • The bank is negotiating with Ripple and LMAX group to qualify RLUSD as collateral for the bank.
  • The planned setup potentially will allow institutions to trade via RLUSD without transferring tokens to the venue.

Standard Chartered has taken another step into stablecoin infrastructure by launching custody support for Ripple USD, or RLUSD, on the XRP Ledger.

Now it is offered to eligible institutional traders from the bank’s Dubai International Financial Centre branch, and a wider collateral integration with Ripple and LMAX Group is underway.

  • Standard Chartered Launches RLUSD Custody on XRPL
  • RLUSD Could Stay in Custody While Supporting Trading
    • Ripple and LMAX Target More Efficient Stablecoin Collateral
    • Full Collateral Integration Is Not Live Yet

Standard Chartered Launches RLUSD Custody on XRPL

Standard Chartered’s digital asset custody infrastructure has now made eligible clients able to hold RLUSD. The service is offered through the bank’s DIFC branch, which is regulated by the Dubai Financial Services Authority.

That provides another way for institutions to gain access to RLUSD, aside from crypto-native custodians. The move is targeted at those looking to gain access to digital asset markets without compromising on the importance of maintaining institutional level practices for long-term custody, governance and risk management, Standard Chartered Inc said.

RLUSD runs on the XRP Ledger, the platform that aims to deliver quick and cheap settlement for DeFi applications.

Read More: OKX Secures Circle, Ripple and Standard Chartered Backing at $25B Valuation

RLUSD Could Stay in Custody While Supporting Trading

The more noteworthy facet of the partnership is the envisioned cross collateral model. Standard Chartered and the LMAX Group plan to enable RLUSD to qualify for specific products and trading services.

According to this design, the client will not be required to transmit their RLUSD to the trading platform. LMAX, on the other hand, would be reimbursed by the bank Standard Chartered for the value of the eligible collateral, with the underlying tokens still held by the bank.

The model should help to mitigate operational risks associated with frequent transfers of assets and increase control around exposure to counterparties for institutions.

Ripple and LMAX Target More Efficient Stablecoin Collateral

Collateral mobility may be as critical to an institution as to the custody. Once the planned integration goes live, companies may potentially be able to keep RLUSD and apply its value throughout the LMAX trading infrastructure.

That could help to better utilize capital by eliminating the need for entities to shift capital from platform to platform. The true use cases for the ripple are where institutions want stablecoins to operate within a known and regulated financial environment, said Ripple.

Read More: Ripple Eyes Türkiye’s $200B Crypto Market as RLUSD and Bank Custody Gain Ground

Full Collateral Integration Is Not Live Yet

Custody service is already in place; however, the RLUSD collateral functionality is still in development at LMAX.

Final documentation, successful testing, regulatory requirements, internal approvals and jurisdictional readiness remain as factors that must be considered before the companies start implementing.

The partnership brings together three separate pieces of infrastructure: Ripple’s stablecoin and XRPL settlement layer, Standard Chartered’s institutional custody platform and LMAX Group’s trading marketplace.

Completed, it would transition the stablecoin to more direct involvement of RLUSD in institutional trading and collateral management, instead of the stablecoin being limited to payments and settlement.

content:
2026-10-14T19:30:00.000+02:00

Wednesday, 14/10/2026 | 17:30 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • The trader argues that BitMEX lacked the UK authorisation required for his perpetual swap trades and is seeking repayment under financial services law.
  • His lawyers are assessing potential claims from other UK-based BitMEX traders; no group claim has been filed.

BitMEX Trader Seeks 324.8 BTC Back, Leaving Other Trades Untouched Of the roughly 2,294 trades Lewis Barber placed on BitMEX, his lawsuit challenges 1,053. All of them lost money.

He wants the exchange’s operator to return the Bitcoin lost on those trades, but is not asking the court to revisit the rest of his trading, according to a claim reviewed by Guardian.

Barber, a British software engineer, is seeking 324.8 Bitcoin or damages of equivalent value from HDR Global Trading Limited, which operated BitMEX. As of October 1, that amounts to £20.4 million.

His trades were placed through five accounts between 2018 and 2022.

Why Barber Seeks Repayment

Barber argues that BitMEX entered into the disputed perpetual swaps without the authorisation required in the UK.

He relies on Section 26 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000, under which a customer may seek the return of money or property transferred under an agreement made during unauthorised regulated activity.

However, the trader applies that argument to the 1,053 losing trades, rather than seeking to unwind every transaction on his accounts.

The court hasn’t yet decided whether the provision covers those trades or how much Barber could recover. Even if an authorisation breach is proven, Section 28 lets a court enforce the agreement, or allow the provider to keep the transferred property, if it considers that just and equitable.

The Dispute over BitMEX’s UK Activity

For Barber’s argument to succeed, the court must also consider BitMEX’s activity in the UK.

His claim says the platform allowed users to select the country as their place of residence and did not block access from there. It also cites a BitMEX advertisement published in The Times in January 2019.

In March 2020, while Barber was still trading, the Financial Conduct Authority warned that BitMEX might be providing financial services or products in the UK without authorisation.

The warning did not determine whether Barber’s particular trades breached UK rules; that question remains part of his case.

Barber’s lawyers at Seladore Legal are inviting other former UK-based BitMEX clients to register their interest. The firm says it will assess each person’s trading history and circumstances before deciding whether they have a potential claim.

Barber is not the only UK crypto-derivatives customer pursuing an authorisation-based claim. As Finance Magnates reported, 1,692 traders have brought a separate lawsuit alleging that Binance sold them derivatives it was not authorised to offer. Neither case has established liability for the exchange concerned.
