title: Federated Hermes Targets $14B Tokenized Fund Market With Prometheum Q1 2027 Launch
summary:
Key Takeaways: Federated Hermes and Prometheum are set to launch the first tokenized fund product in Q1 2027. Prometheum will distribute, hold, clear and settle on the regulated U.S. broker-dealer
The post Federated Hermes Targets $14B Tokenized Fund Market With Prometheum Q1 2027 Launch appeared fi...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Federated Hermes and Prometheum are set to launch the first tokenized fund product in Q1 2027.
  • Prometheum will distribute, hold, clear and settle on the regulated U.S. broker-dealer platforms.
  • The partnership aims to fund the money market fund and the tokenized Treasury worth over USD 14 billion already onchain.

Federated Hermes is teaming up with Prometheum to get a tokenized investment fund onto the traditional brokerage channels in the U.S. The firms would like brokers and financial advisers to be one way investors can get into blockchain-based securities instead of just crypto-native platforms.

Today we announced a strategic partnership with Federated Hermes, Inc. to distribute tokenized securities through traditional broker-dealer channels.

We believe this will provide product issuers the blueprint for how tokenized funds will reach mainstream investors through the regulated intermediaries they already rely on.

Over $14B in tokenized U.S. Treasury and money market funds alone are on-chain, per https://t.co/9jzdtWoVDT — but almost none of it is accessible through traditional brokerage accounts. ProFinancial will support the distribution of the tokenized products, and Prometheum Capital will custody, clear, and settle these products. Any authorized broker-dealer that clears through us can begin to offer tokenized products to clients without building its own crypto asset infrastructure.

Read the full announcement here: https://t.co/SAHHIVEjQO

#Tokenization #cryptoassets #BrokerDealers

— Prometheum (@PrometheumInc) October 13, 2026

  • Federated Hermes Plans Tokenized Fund Launch in Q1 2027
  • Broker-Dealers Can Access Tokenized Products Without Building Crypto Infrastructure
    • $14B Tokenized Fund Market Gets Traditional Distribution Route
    • Prometheum Builds Full Stack for Tokenized Securities

Federated Hermes Plans Tokenized Fund Launch in Q1 2027

The first product of the collaboration is slated for the market in Q1 of 2027.

With assets of $911.6 billion as of June 30, 2026, Federated Hermes will supply expertise in investment management and tokenized products.

Prometheum will provide regulatory infrastructure to distribute and service them. The structure is designed to take the same kinds of fund/broker relationships that many U.S. investors have for traditional funds and apply them to blockchain-based funds.

Read More: SEC Clears Path for Tokenized Stocks With 5-Year Onchain Trading Exemption

Broker-Dealers Can Access Tokenized Products Without Building Crypto Infrastructure

Issuing and distributing will be undertaken by Prometheum’s ProFinancial subsidiary while handling the custody, clearing and settlement will be undertaken by Prometheum Capital.

Without a need for a digital-asset custody and settlement system, such broker-dealers could then offer tokenized products to clients through a clearinghouse facilitated by Prometheum Capital.

That should help remove one of the largest hurdles to tokenizing assets: distribution.

There are numerous tokenized funds on blockchain networks, though many of these were only available through specialist platforms and not the usual brokerage accounts.

$14B Tokenized Fund Market Gets Traditional Distribution Route

There is already over $14 billion of tokenized U.S. Treasury and money market funds onchain, says Prometheum. The partnership is designed to give that growing asset class a more direct path into regulated brokerage infrastructure.

Blockchain-based access to traditional investments products is attracting demand from broker-dealers and registered investment advisers, said Federated Hermes.

Instead of replacing established financial intermediaries, the model keeps broker-dealers, custodians and clearing firms at the center of the transaction flow.

Read More: OKX Eyes 63 U.S. Stocks in Major Tokenized Trading Expansion

Prometheum Builds Full Stack for Tokenized Securities

Prometheum’s larger overall structure features multiple regulated entities with various stages of the securities lifecycle.

ProFinancial is responsible for issuance and distribution, Prometheum Capital is a custody and clearing service and Prometheum ATS has registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as a digital transfer agent.

That entity provides the company with a playbook to follow for tokenized securities from issuance to custody to eventual trade. At Federated Hermes we are able to add to that the scale that we have, we are over 11,000 institutions and intermediaries globally.

If the launch of Q1 2027 is as expected, the partnership could prove the capability of tokenized funds to successfully get onto investor investable networks beyond cryptocurrency exchange platforms.

title: OCC report finds debanking efforts tied to crypto activities
summary: The report from the US banking regulator did not include specific examples of debanking related to crypto, but mentioned it alongside ties to oil, gas and firearms.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedOct 14, 2026

The report from the US banking regulator did not include specific examples of debanking related to crypto, but mentioned it alongside ties to oil, gas and firearms.

The US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) released a report on debanking efforts, including ties to digital assets as activities that influenced banks to limit financial services.

In a report released Wednesday, the OCC said certain banks had “public and nonpublic policies” restricting services for many industries, including oil and gas, tobacco, firearms and digital assets. According to the banking regulator, the report was in accordance with an August 2025 executive order from US President Donald Trump to prevent what he called “unlawful debanking.”

“Many institutions also placed restrictions on banking digital asset activities, including on issuers, exchanges, or administrators, often attributed to financial crime considerations,” said the OCC.

In November 2024, more than 30 tech and crypto executives claimed to have been denied access to banking services. Many in the crypto industry unofficially dubbed the effort as “Operation Chokepoint 2.0” after the Obama-era initiative to fight fraud and money laundering facilitated by banks.

However, Wednesday’s 47-page report did not include specific examples of debanking relating to digital asset activities. The OCC said it had been “unable to quantify on a comprehensive basis the full extent of debanking or alleged debanking actions” based on a review of nine major banks, and the agency’s head, Jonathan Gould, focused largely on the report’s claims around debanking due to ties to coal and firearms.

“These decisions were not based on financial risk,” said Gould, referencing the debanking due to connections to coal. “Instead, banks cited concerns about negative headlines, public protests, and the perceived reputational consequences of supporting the industry.”

The 2025 executive order from Trump followed calls from many in the industry surrounding claims -- including “Operation Chokepoint 2.0” -- that the US government under former President Joe Biden may have influenced financial institutions into cutting off crypto firms from certain services. 

Related: Fed seeks feedback on proposal critics say could end Operation Chokepoint 2.0

title: Axi Clients Can Now Ask Claude to Place Trades in Their MetaTrader Accounts
summary:
Axi said today (Wednesday) that eligible clients can connect their MetaTrader 5 (MT5) accounts to Claude, Anthropic's AI assistant, and use it to place trades. The link runs through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), an open standard for connecting AI tools to outside data and services.
Through Claud...
content:
2026-10-14T18:54:00.000+02:00

Wednesday, 14/10/2026 | 16:54 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • The connector, still in alpha testing, needs the client’s approval in chat before any order goes through.
  • It runs on Claude’s free plan, while TradeStation asks for Claude Pro and a $10,000 balance.

Axi said today (Wednesday) that eligible clients can connect their MetaTrader 5 (MT5) accounts to Claude, Anthropic's AI assistant, and use it to place trades. The link runs through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), an open standard for connecting AI tools to outside data and services.

Through Claude, clients can check live prices, open, modify and close positions, place pending orders and adjust stop-loss and take-profit levels, according to the connector's website. Axi describes the service as being in alpha testing.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The entry cost on the AI side is zero. Axi says the connector works on Claude's free plan, which allows one custom connector, while TradeStation requires a Claude Pro subscription and a $10,000 account balance for its MCP link.

Axi built the integration on MT5 , whose developer MetaQuotes added native AI agents and MCP support in a July beta.

Approval in Chat, With an Exception

Any trade or order action needs the client's explicit approval in the chat before it goes through, the connector's website says.

Leverate built the same step into its own product. Its MCP for Traders restates each order and waits for a yes in the trader's AI app, and brokers must switch the feature on.

Axi's help center adds that Claude "is not an automated strategy or Expert Advisor (EA)." It acts only when a client asks, unless the client has set a specific action to "Always allow" in Claude's permission settings.

Interactive Brokers lets Claude draft trades but requires manual sign-off on each order, a setup it launched in June for equities and ETFs.

How Far Rivals Let AI Trade

"AI is creating new opportunities to rethink how traders interact with technology," Axi Global Head of Sales Santiago Vazquez-Munoz said in the announcement.

ThinkMarkets' ChelseaAI server lets AI models execute orders on ThinkTrader but not access funds, the broker said when it launched in June.

Match-Trade opened its MCP to retail traders on October 5, with an option for compatible clients to require approval for each action.

CMC Markets went the other way. Its ChatGPT link for UK clients is read-only and cannot trade, change orders or move money.

Who Can Connect

Only active MT5 accounts, verified or unverified, can connect. Accounts that run only on MT4 or the Axi trading platform are excluded.

Clients add Axi as a custom connector in Claude, enter the broker's MCP address and approve access by logging in with their Axi credentials. Axi support can guide them but cannot set up the connection on their behalf.

The help center also says Claude is not a financial advisor and that its answers are not trade recommendations. Axi said the integration does not remove trading risk and that clients remain responsible for their trading decisions.

title: Coinbase Joins 4-Day Crackdown on West Africa Crypto Scams and Asset Freezes
summary:
Key Takeaways: Coinbase participated in a four-day assault of scam networks in West Africa in London. Its Global Intelligence team tracked illicit crypto activity, aided asset freeze operations, and provided
The post Coinbase Joins 4-Day Crackdown on West Africa Crypto Scams and Asset Freezes appear...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Coinbase participated in a four-day assault of scam networks in West Africa in London.
  • Its Global Intelligence team tracked illicit crypto activity, aided asset freeze operations, and provided intelligence sharing with law enforcement.
  • The impersonation scams included fake crypto investments and staged video-call arrests by the police.

Coinbase has joined a coordinated enforcement effort aimed at disrupting scam networks expanding into West Africa.

During an operation in London, Oct. 6 – 9, the exchange collaborated with the UK’s National Crime Agency, the U.S. Department of Justice’s Scam Center Strike Force, Tech Against Scams and other international partners.

  • Coinbase Traces Crypto Flows Behind Scam Networks
  • Scammers Used Fake Investments and Staged Arrests
    • West Africa Emerges as a New Focus
    • Coinbase Keeps Pressure on Crypto Fraud Networks

Coinbase Traces Crypto Flows Behind Scam Networks

Coinbase’s Global Intelligence team was dedicated to tracking illegal funds related to scam operations. The company said investigators helped trace funds, supported asset freezes and could help ongoing criminal investigations for the company.

The work integrated blockchain transaction data with other elements of the digital ecosystem, such as fake social media profiles, messaging accounts, and fraudulent sites.

That can aid investigators connect activity that might appear disjoint when it shows on various platforms. The purpose was not just to shut off individual accounts, Coinbase said, but also to uncover the underlying systems that are being leveraged to mask the movement of stolen assets and run scams.

Read More: Coinbase Unveils AiFi After $100M in x402 Transactions, Targeting AI Agent Payments

Scammers Used Fake Investments and Staged Arrests

The operation was directed at various aspects of fraud. Coinbase identified fake cryptocurrency investment schemes, a virtual arrest via video call designed to flex the power cords, and criminals posing as law enforcement officers.

Often scams are executed over numerous services until any funds end up in a crypto wallet or exchange. The victim might first be contacted via social media, then switched to a private messaging service after which they are asked to pay using financial channels.

That’s why enterprise-level intelligence sharing is particularly valuable when the investigators are trying to uncover the entire scheme.

West Africa Emerges as a New Focus

Effort to crack down on scam compounds across Southeast Asia has compelled certain criminal organisations to expand their activities to other global areas such as West Africa, Coinbase said.

Every effort has been made to disrupt networks that could have built stronger infrastructure in London. Members focused on the accounts, communications and payment mechanisms that facilitate scam activity.

The work also signals another trend for tech vendors, financial institutions, telecom and security organizations all getting more involved with investigations, coordinated efforts.

Coinbase Keeps Pressure on Crypto Fraud Networks

Coinbase has previously tracked down scams in a similar fashion. The company has explained that its part in the latest campaign was ensuring that blockchain intelligence could be merged with data collected by third party organizations and would enable police to respond quicker.

Vice President Leah Bressack described the strategy as sustained pressure on criminal networks that move between regions and platforms.

Coinbase said it plans to continue working with Tech Against Scams and law enforcement partners to trace illicit funds, disrupt active schemes and support investigations against the groups operating them.

title: Kalshi CEO says state-led oversight of U.S. prediction markets would push them out
summary: CEO Tarek Mansour said he feels "pretty good" about the pending outcome of the current legal fight over who has the right to regulate prediction markets.
content:
Oct 14, 2026, 12:34 p.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

  • The CEO of prediction markets firm Kalshi, Tarek Mansour, said that if the U.S. court side with states who claim gambling authorities over such businesses, they’ll be forced offshore.
  • Though a couple of federal courts have issued decisions against his view, Mansour suggested he feels “pretty good” about his company’s legal standing in the U.S.

ARLINGTON, Va. — The CEO of Kalshi, the company at the center of a high-profile legal battle over the future of prediction markets in the U.S., said the clash won't ultimately decide whether the rapidly growing industry is overseen by states or a federal agency, but whether it's overseen by the feds here or is forced overseas.

"We feel pretty good about where we stand overall," Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour said Wednesday at the DC Fintech Week event near Washington.

Mansour rejected arguments that sports betting — the explosively growing element of the event-contracts space — doesn't have significant economic consequences that justify the trades' status as federally regulated financial contracts.

"The notion that sports does not have economic consequence is ludicrous," he said.

A growing list of states have challenged Kalshi and other prediction markets firms in court, accusing them of engaging in illegal sports wagering that belongs under the authority of state gambling regulators. But Kalshi and the federal regulator of its exchange, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, have countered in courts that the federal agency is the appropriate sole watchdog of prediction markets.

So far, the dispute has risen to a number of federal appellate courts, where the courts have now split, with one major ruling on Kalshi's side and two backing the states' view. As a result, New Jersey asked the U.S. Supreme Court to take the case, and prominent groups have been sharing their views with the high court, including the National Football League.

Mansour said, "It's not a choice of state versus federal market. It's a choice of whether prediction markets exist in the U.S. or whether they go offshore."

He argued that he's considered Kalshi's regulatory relationship since its beginnings, and "it really elegantly fit under definitions of commodity." He said the Commodity Exchange Act was a "truly beautiful statue" that allowed a shift from agricultural futures to oil and metals to less tangible financial products like swaps.

Mansour also responded Wednesday to accusations of inflated trading volume in bitcoin and ether perpetual-futures markets on his platform. He said that "there's a lot of crazy" on social media site X, formerly Twitter. The questions focused on often-recurring trade sizes that represented a significant portion of Kalshi's volume. Mansour pointed again at the Washington event to fixed-size orders from market makers.

title: Ripple and Privy Bring XRP Wallets to XRPL After $1T Moved Across 8M Accounts
summary:
Key Takeaways: With the collaboration of Ripple, Privy offers programmable wallet infrastructure to the XRP Ledger. Developers can create and develop using XRP, RLUSD and any other assets on the
The post Ripple and Privy Bring XRP Wallets to XRPL After $1T Moved Across 8M Accounts appeared first on ...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • With the collaboration of Ripple, Privy offers programmable wallet infrastructure to the XRP Ledger.
  • Developers can create and develop using XRP, RLUSD and any other assets on the XRPL and develop embedded and server-side wallets.
  • Over the course of the last 14 years, XRPL has achieved more than $1 trillion in value transferred and over 8 million funded accounts.

Ripple and Privy are building wallet capabilities on the XRP Ledger for payments, stablecoin products and automatic transactions. The integration is designed to remove much of the wallet-management complexity that can slow crypto adoption inside fintech apps and payment platforms.

  • Privy Brings Programmable Wallets to XRP Ledger
  • Server-Side Wallets Open the Door to Agent Payments
    • XRP and RLUSD Gain More Developer Infrastructure
    • Ripple and Privy Plan Deeper Wallet Controls

Privy Brings Programmable Wallets to XRP Ledger

Currently, every XRPL user must have to install and use a standalone crypto wallet, but with Privy’s API this will be eliminated.

It will also enable developers to sign XRPL transactions on Privy’s infrastructure and develop apps based on XRP, Ripple USD and other digital assets issued on XRPL.

Embedded wallets could bring stablecoin payments more into the realm of traditional fintech experiences for consumer facing products. Users don’t have to handle private keys when using the app in normal conditions.

Meanwhile, Privy will allow for private-key and seed-phrase exports, which will aid users in retaining ownership of their private keys.

Read More: Ripple Eyes Türkiye’s $200B Crypto Market as RLUSD and Bank Custody Gain Ground

Server-Side Wallets Open the Door to Agent Payments

The partnership also aims at server side wallets that enable software agents to collect funds and conduct transactions automatically. Privy mentions x402 payments, a standard that is being developed for machine-to-machine and automated commerce.

That gives developers the opportunity of creating AI agents or standalone applications that can transfer funds to others, get funds from them, or interact with the blockchain financial services without human intervention every time.

XRP and RLUSD Gain More Developer Infrastructure

With Ripple prioritizing XRPL’s entry into payments and tokenized finance, the integration seems to be just another development blanket over the XRP and RLUSD layers. According to Privy, XRPL is in its 14+ years of operation with more than 8 million funded accounts. The network has also received a total of over $1 trillion transferred.

The network is fast and has low transaction fees, which makes it suitable for payment-related applications that need transactions to be cheap and fast. privy’s tools might enable that capacity to be adopted more easily by fintech products, requiring developers to create wallet infrastructure from scratch.

Read More: Ripple Powers Absa Digital Asset Custody Launch for Africa’s $205B Crypto Market

Ripple and Privy Plan Deeper Wallet Controls

The two companies are also working on some additional features for the integration, which currently centers on wallet creation, asset support and transaction signing. The future development of the policy controls and gas sponsorship will continue, said Privy.

Policy controls could provide greater powers of regulation for developers when it comes to the transactions possible with certain wallets, and gas sponsorship can eliminate yet another level of complexity for end users when using the blockchain.

The payment providers and developers creating automated applications could find that the combination makes XRPL wallets more of a financial tool than a standalone crypto wallet.

title: Kraken Parent Company Payward to Buy Saldo Bank in European Banking Push
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Kraken Parent Company Payward to Buy Saldo Bank in European Banking Push
Top crypto exchange Kraken is pushing to offer other services other than digital assets. 
This post Kraken Parent Company Payward to Buy Saldo Bank in European Banking Push first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine a...
content:
Payward, the parent company of crypto exchange Kraken, has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Saldo Bank, gaining an EU banking license and a footprint across five European markets.

Payward is buying Saldo Finance Oy, a Finnish holding company whose subsidiary, Saldo Bank UAB, is a digital-first specialized bank licensed in Lithuania. The bank operates in Lithuania, Finland, Sweden and Germany, with a passport into the Netherlands. 

Payward did not reveal the financial terms of the deal, which is expected to close in 2027, subject to regulatory approvals.

It comes as Kraken, like other crypto exchanges, pushes further into the traditional finance world, allowing users to trade stocks, bonds and other assets. The company has sold its app as a “primary account for everything.”

“A regulated EU bank is the piece that lets us serve European clients the way a primary financial institution should: one place to hold assets, move them freely, and put them to work,” said Arjun Sethi, Payward’s co-CEO. “We are starting in the EU, and the ambition is global.”

Payward said that once completed, the acquisition is expected to let Payward Banking offer interest on deposits, SME and consumer loans, credit cards, and banking-as-a-service tools such as card issuance, SEPA payments access and embedded lending for partners. 

Saldo already offers retail term deposits in all four of its operating markets, consumer lending in Lithuania, Finland and Sweden, and a credit card in Finland.

Payward says it already holds a Federal Reserve limited-purpose master account in the U.S. and an e-money license from the Central Bank of Ireland, and has originated more than $2 billion in loans.

The deal comes shortly after Payward this week announced plans to launch in the UAE following full approval from Dubai’s Virtual Asset Regulatory Authority. 

In September, Bloomberg reported  that Nasdaq Inc. was investing $100 million in Payward at a $21 billion valuation, citing people familiar with the matter. Payward and SoFi Technologies also recently agreed to route SoFi customers’ crypto orders through Kraken Prime, Kraken’s prime brokerage arm.

summary:

From November 12, the EBA will directly s...
content:
2026-10-14T18:27:24.215+02:00

Wednesday, 14/10/2026 | 16:27 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • The European Banking Authority named it a significant e-money token, the first of 45 in the bloc.
  • From November 12 the authority, not France’s ACPR, will check the token’s reserves, capital and liquidity.

The European Banking Authority (EBA) classified Circle's USDC as a significant e-money token under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) today (Wednesday). It is the first of the 45 e-money tokens notified in the European Union to receive the label.

From November 12, the EBA will directly supervise USDC's own funds, reserve of assets, liquidity and recovery and redemption plans. Those tasks move from France's Prudential Control and Resolution Authority (ACPR), which licensed Circle as an e-money institution in July 2024.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The decision hands an EU-level supervisor the reserves behind a token Circle said had $73.3 billion in circulation worldwide at the end of June, up 19% from a year earlier.

The largest dollar stablecoin is absent from regulated EU venues. Tether did not seek MiCA authorization for USDT, which major regulated platforms delisted before the July 1 deadline.

What It Means for Platforms Listing USDC

From November, exchanges and brokers that offer USDC in the EU will list a token whose reserves are supervised by the EBA, rather than by a national authority.

Kraken expanded support for USDC and EURC in September 2025 to cut conversion fees for its users.

Binance went further. In September, it bought a $100 million stake in Circle alongside a five-year USDC agreement under which Circle pays the exchange monthly incentives tied to USDC balances.

USDC supply has moved both ways this year. Circulation stood at $77.0 billion at the end of March before falling to $73.3 billion by the end of June, according to Circle's quarterly results.

Circle cited Visa Onchain Analytics data putting USDC at 63% of stablecoin transaction volume in the first quarter.

Who Supervises What From November 12

USDC will fall under the dual supervision MiCA sets for significant tokens. The ACPR keeps governance, qualifying holdings, fit-and-proper assessments, outsourcing and conflicts of interest.

The EBA said it and the ACPR would work closely to ensure a smooth transition. The authority reassesses every year whether a token still meets the criteria for significance.

Under MiCA, a token is significant when it meets at least three of seven criteria. They include more than 10 million holders, an issued value or reserve above EUR 5 billion, and more than 2.5 million transactions worth over EUR 500 million a day.

The other criteria cover the issuer's international reach, its links to the financial system and whether it issues other tokens while providing crypto services.

The EBA did not say which criteria USDC met.

Circle's euro token, EURC, is issued under the same French license. The decision applies only to USDC.

A Token Issued on Both Sides of the Atlantic

USDC is issued in the EU by Circle Internet Financial Europe SAS and in the US by Circle Internet Financial, LLC, the EBA noted.

The EBA has a memorandum of understanding with the New York State Department of Financial Services (NYDFS) on cross-border stablecoin supervision. It announced the agreement on June 2, saying it covers issuers it supervises directly under MiCA.

The agreement provides for information exchange, mutual assistance in ongoing supervision and coordination in a crisis. The EBA said it had assessed the New York regulator's confidentiality rules as equivalent to those under MiCA, a condition for sharing confidential information.

In the US, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) gave Circle final approval in July for a national trust bank, which will start with custody for Circle and its affiliates.

A stablecoin issued in one jurisdiction and used in another still falls under separate US, UK and EU regimes, Hedera Chief Policy Officer Nilmini Rubin wrote in a FinanceMagnates.com column in August.

title: Standard Chartered pushes $2T stablecoin forecast to 2030 as transaction volumes grow
summary: The bank identified four distinct stablecoin markets, with USDC leading payments and AI transactions as competition intensifies over reserve yields.
content:
Standard Chartered says stablecoin transaction activity continues to grow even as the market’s overall value has stalled, suggesting existing stablecoins are circulating more frequently rather than new supply driving growth.

In a report shared with Cointelegraph, the bank said it now expects stablecoin market capitalization to reach $2 trillion by 2030, two years later than initially projected, after the market plateaued at roughly $309 billion this year.

Geoffrey Kendrick, StanChart’s head of digital assets research, said stablecoin usage continues to expand despite slower supply growth, with existing stablecoins changing hands more frequently as their use cases diversify.

Kendrick identified four distinct markets, each with different competitive dynamics. Tether’s USDt (USDT) dominates emerging-market savings, while Circle’s USDC (USDC) leads developed-market payments. USDC and Ethena’s USDe have established strong positions in crypto trading, while USDC also leads the much smaller market for transactions between AI agents.

The bank expects the most intense competition in developed market payments, where challengers such as USDG, M^0 and multibank stablecoin networks are pursuing alternatives to existing payment infrastructure.

According to Kendrick, how issuers and payment networks divide the yield generated by stablecoin reserves could ultimately determine which competitors gain market share.

Related: Crypto’s billions are back, but the premiums aren’t

US regulatory and accounting changes could shape stablecoin use

Standard Chartered’s revised forecast comes as regulatory and accounting developments in the United States could influence how businesses use stablecoins.

Since the GENIUS Act passed in 2025, US regulators have proposed rules governing stablecoin issuance, reserve requirements and consumer protections. Some measures have also clarified the limits of those protections, including a Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) proposal that would exclude stablecoin holders from pass-through deposit insurance.

The Treasury Department has also advanced implementation of the law. In August, it proposed rules restricting stablecoin issuance in the United States to federally or state-authorized issuers, with the licensing requirements expected to take effect in January 2027.

Separately, in August, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB), which sets US accounting standards, proposed an update that could affect how companies report certain stablecoins on their balance sheets.

Blockchain payments company Tempo said the proposed changes could make it easier for businesses to use stablecoins for payments and settlement without introducing additional accounting complications.

Related: Crypto Biz: Wall Street and crypto fight for the same turf

title: Standard Chartered Debuts Bitcoin Trading For Wealthy UAE Clients
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Standard Chartered Debuts Bitcoin Trading For Wealthy UAE Clients 
The service allows affluent clients to buy bitcoin via their bank accounts. 
This post Standard Chartered Debuts Bitcoin Trading For Wealthy UAE Clients  first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew D...
content:
British multinational Standard Chartered on Wednesday announced a bitcoin trading service for affluent clients in the United Arab Emirates. 

The service is the first such service offered by an international bank in the UAE, Standard Chartered said. 

It comes after the bank last month debuted bitcoin trading for institutional clients in the Arab nation. Standard Chartered became one of the first global banks to enter the spot crypto trading space when in 2025 it set up a trading desk for bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies in London. 

“As client interest in digital assets continues to grow, this launch represents a significant milestone for Standard Chartered as we bring digital assets into our core wealth offering,” said Samir Subberwal, Standard Chartered’s global head of wealth solutions, retail products, data and analytics.

“With digital assets moving into mainstream wealth conversations, clients are increasingly looking not only for access, but also for the security, trust and confidence that comes from investing through a regulated and trusted institution.” 

Rola Abu Manneh, Standard Chartered’s chief executive officer UAE, Middle East and Pakistan, added: “We are proud to be the first international bank in the UAE to launch a cryptocurrency trading offering.”

The service will allow clients to buy bitcoin via their bank accounts. No third-party apps or wallets will be needed, the bank said. 

Standard Chartered said it will manage end-to-end custody and settlement through a closed-loop model, reducing exposure to third-party wallet risks. 

The British bank is expanding its crypto-related offerings worldwide. Earlier this month, it said it had plans to offer crypto custody services for institutional clients in Singapore.

Standard Chartered already offers the service in the UAE, Luxembourg, and Hong Kong.

Banks worldwide are integrating or offering bitcoin-related products and services. 

A number of U.S. and European banks have started offering crypto-related services by custodying assets for institutions. Others are offering trading via their flagship apps. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: The Undercurrent: Three European Artists on Making Money Visible
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

The Undercurrent: Three European Artists on Making Money Visible
Ahead of Bitcoin Amsterdam, ZETRA, RYR, and Cypherpunk Now reflect on the cultural roots of bitcoin, the changing meaning of money, and a movement confronting its own institutional success.
This post The Undercurrent:...
content:
Amsterdam helped lay the foundations of modern finance, but its artists were among its earliest critics. When speculative bubbles burst across Europe in 1720, Amsterdam printers and satirists responded with The Great Mirror of Folly, a collection of engravings and plays exposing the excesses of financial speculation.

Nearly three centuries later, the city hosted another monetary experiment. David Chaum, the cryptographer whose work on anonymous communication helped lay the groundwork for the cypherpunk movement, came to Amsterdam in the 1980s to work at CWI, the Dutch national research institute for mathematics and computer science. Around 1990, he founded DigiCash to develop private electronic cash. The company went bankrupt in 1998, a decade before bitcoin, but the dream of digital money was already taking shape.

Last year at Bitcoin Amsterdam, BMAG exhibited The Waterworks of Money, in which Dutch artist Carlijn Kingma, working with financial journalist Thomas Bollen and researcher Martijn Jeroen van der Linden, depicted the monetary system as a vast irrigation network, with some areas flooded by liquidity while others remain dry. The drawing makes a complex financial system legible, exposing the mechanisms through which money is created, distributed, and concentrated.

This tradition of questioning money and making its hidden dimensions visible continues in the work of three European artists exhibiting at Bitcoin Amsterdam this November. ZETRA, RYR, and Cypherpunk Now draw from graffiti, political printmaking, hacker culture, and early bitcoin communities to explore the changing meaning of money.

Martin Fischer joined the Prague art collective Ztohoven in 2003, a group known for inserting a fictional nuclear explosion into a live Czech Television broadcast. In 2014, the collective opened Paralelní Polis, a hackerspace whose café accepted only bitcoin, and Fischer designed its logo. As he told Bitcoin Magazine’s Aaron van Wirdum in 2020, the arrival of a screen-printing press the following year prompted him to produce his first prints. Since 2020, he has worked under the name Cypherpunk Now, developing a visual record of bitcoin’s evolving culture.

RYR and ZETRA both emerged from Germany’s graffiti scene but approach money from different directions. RYR uses currency itself as material, making paper from shredded banknotes, pigment from their ashes, and concrete grenades filled with shredded cash that he calls “artifacts from the future.” ZETRA, who began painting in the early 1990s and discovered bitcoin in 2017, examines what money can buy. His TOMATOSOUP paintings revisit Andy Warhol’s iconic Campbell’s Soup Cans to chart changing prices in dollars and bitcoin, while THE BIP39 SERIES explores the 2,048 words used in bitcoin wallet recovery phrases, including 1206/NOTE, a collaboration with Polymerbit.

Bitcoin has shaped these artists’ practices, their livelihoods, and the communities around them. Its growing acceptance by banks, investment funds, and corporations has also prompted some difficult questions about the movement’s original ideals and where its culture is heading.

BMAG: Andy Warhol turned Campbell’s soup into an icon of consumer culture, taking an ordinary commodity and elevating it into fine art. Your TOMATOSOUP series returns to that image but introduces something Warhol largely left outside the frame: the changing value of money itself. How did the idea of reworking Warhol’s Campbell’s Soup Cans first come about, and do viewers immediately recognize the commentary on inflation?

ZETRA: We frequently see iPhones and houses in our bitcoin Twitter timelines, showing how they become cheaper in BTC terms. I thought it would be fun to take something from art history instead, something more visually appealing, like Warhol’s iconic Campbell’s Soup Can.

For my TOMATOSOUP painting, I used real stickers placed on the can to show how the price of soup has increased in USD over the past decades, compared with the lower prices we might expect in BTC terms in the decades to come.

Bitcoiners looking at TOMATOSOUP generally understand it immediately. They know they’re in a better position as the purchasing power of fiat money continues to decline through inflation. Other viewers usually need a bit of explanation, and I’m always happy to help them understand.

BMAG: In THE BIP39 SERIES, you draw from the 2,048 words used to generate bitcoin wallet recovery phrases, turning ordinary words into artworks with a deeper significance for bitcoin holders. Can you unpack the different layers of inspiration behind the series and what they reveal about bitcoin, language, and the ownership of money for someone unfamiliar with these concepts?

ZETRA: Everyone who moves their precious sats into cold storage encounters 12 or 24 of these significant words, often early in their journey as a bitcoin newcomer. As mentioned, there are 2,048 words in a carefully curated list representing the power of self-custody.

I started going through the words one by one, imagining how each could be visualized in a physical form: the key visual for the word, its corresponding number, the style, and the medium I would choose. There are millions of possibilities for bringing these words to life through bitcoin art.

1044/LIST was the obvious choice to kick off THE BIP39 SERIES. Naturally, it features all 2,048 words presented as a list. As an ’80s kid, I had to choose 1638/SMILE as the second piece: a proper yellow smiley face, with the number 1638 in place of the eyes. It’s a fine art print on Alu-Dibond beneath a 6 mm acrylic glass cover. So clean.

Another work in the series is 0388/CORN, an obvious homage to Warhol once again. THE BIP39 SERIES will be an ongoing project for many years to come.

BMAG: You shred banknotes into paper and burn them to produce pigment. Artists have long manipulated currency to question where its value resides, but your work goes a step further by making destruction part of the creative process. Is there a contradiction in destroying money to create an artwork that may ultimately be worth much more?

RYR: Money is essentially a narrative system built on collective belief and obedience. It has worked for hundreds of years because we collectively agree on the story it tells and the value it represents. I’ve always been fascinated by that idea, particularly how something as ordinary as a banknote can carry so much meaning, authority, and perceived value.

I was looking for a different way to tell that story, both conceptually and physically. Back in 2017, I had an exhibition title in mind: To Cut a Long Story Short. I liked the cheekiness of it, especially in relation to money and the stories we attach to it. Shredding banknotes became a very literal interpretation of that title, but it also opened up an entirely new artistic medium for me.

Ultimately, I’m not simply destroying money. I’m taking an existing story, cutting it into pieces, and using those pieces to tell a new one.

BMAG: Your concrete weapons are presented as relics from a future in which the fiat wars have already ended. Yet bitcoin is increasingly held through the very financial institutions it was designed to circumvent. Is that a victory for the movement, or have the institutions simply absorbed the alternative?

RYR: I think that’s precisely what makes the story so interesting. When I created the concrete weapons, I imagined a future in which the traditional financial system had already fought its battle for survival. The weapons had become fossils, archaeological artifacts from a monetary conflict that future generations might struggle to understand.

My concrete weapons represent a future in which that battle is already history. Whether bitcoin ultimately wins or becomes part of the very system it challenged remains to be seen.

BMAG: Much of your work is made from the physical remains of money, at a time when currency is becoming increasingly digital and invisible. Do you think people are losing something in their understanding of money as it disappears from everyday physical experience?

RYR: I think we’re losing a physical connection to money, but not necessarily our understanding of it. Money has always been a narrative built on collective trust, whether printed on paper or represented by numbers on a screen. What fascinates me is how something as abstract as value can be represented by a physical object.

I don’t necessarily believe that art has to be authentic or entirely original. Almost everything has been done before. To me, art is a wonderfully human, almost plebeian way of expressing an opinion and giving ideas a physical voice.

Bitcoin will likely evolve into a much broader and increasingly regulated financial asset, but I hope its grassroots culture and artistic identity remain visible. That’s something my fellow artists and I will continue to contribute to, preserving the spirit of a movement that was cultural long before it became institutional.

BMAG: Paralelní Polis wasn’t just a place to discuss alternative monetary systems or a hacker meetup; its café was one of the first to adopt bitcoin as money. What were the early years of Paralelní Polis like, and what has your own experience been selling artwork for bitcoin?

Martin Fischer: Paralelní Polis was founded in 2014, during a bear market. The funny thing is, none of us who founded it even knew what a bear market was. We didn’t think of bitcoin as something that could make us rich. We saw it as uncensorable money and understood the changes it could bring to society. There was no speculation involved, and that’s what made those early days so great.

I sold my first screenprint for bitcoin in 2017, almost ten years ago, and many more since then. But practically every sale was a matter of survival. I spent most of the bitcoin I earned financing my next projects and continuing to make art.

I never managed to accumulate much bitcoin, but looking back, it gave me something far more valuable than investment returns: the freedom to remain an independent artist.

BMAG: Political printmaking has a long history in Europe, from Amsterdam’s financial satires of 1720 to twentieth-century protest posters. Your work emerged from Ztohoven, a collective that famously hacked a live television broadcast to show a fictional nuclear explosion—an audacious intervention, even by today’s standards. Ztohoven challenged institutions through disruption, while bitcoin uses game theory and economic incentives to create an alternative. Do you see bitcoin as a continuation of that same spirit of intervention, and your prints as an extension of it?

Martin Fischer: I think there’s a connection, but I wouldn’t say it’s exactly the same thing. With Ztohoven, we used art to question authority, challenge institutions, and expose how easily reality can be manipulated. Bitcoin doesn’t need to make a statement or provoke anyone. It simply offers an alternative that works without asking anyone for permission. That’s a much more interesting form of disruption to me.

But today, bitcoin has become so corporate and so intertwined with traditional banking that it’s hard to still see it as an anti-establishment movement. I don’t see this as a betrayal of its original ideals, but rather as a natural consequence of its success. That doesn’t mean I like where things are going.

What’s strange is that bitcoin’s fundamental principles haven’t really changed, but the way people perceive and use it certainly has.

And my screenprints? I still work with the original idea of separating money from the state while exploring the myths, memes, and legends of the bitcoin age. That’s what I enjoy most.

BMAG: Your Amsterdam presentation brings together more than a decade of work documenting bitcoin’s evolution from an underground movement to an increasingly institutionalized financial system. Looking across those prints today, has the movement changed more than you expected, or has your own perspective changed? Which of your prints are your favorites?

Martin Fischer: I like remembering the old days, when we were all part of the same tribe and our main enemy was Faketoshi.

Today? We have culture wars over JPEGs, Ordinals, BIPs, OP_RETURN, over what’s spam and what should or shouldn’t belong on bitcoin. What makes me saddest is that people who once fought together against censorship and for freedom now spend enormous amounts of energy fighting each other over what others should or shouldn’t be allowed to do with bitcoin.

Maybe it’s a natural consequence of bitcoin’s success. The bitcoin community has changed enormously, and so has my perspective on it. I’m definitely much more skeptical today of the idea that technology alone can automatically change society for the better.

As for my favorite works, Bitcoin Meteorite is definitely one of them. In this piece, I reworked the meme of banking dinosaurs watching their own extinction, incorporating the abstract from the Bitcoin white paper. It gave me my fifteen minutes of fame when Max Keiser and Stacy Herbert brought it into the spotlight.

Then there’s Cypherpunks of the World. This project is important to me not only as a celebration of the cypherpunks and their legacy, but also because of its complexity. It started as a series of original collages, continued through handmade screenprints, and eventually evolved into animated NFTs and a virtual gallery. It’s one of my most elaborate projects, connecting different techniques and media while staying true to the original idea.

Among my more recent works, I really like Out of Order from 2023. It’s an incredibly detailed screenprint, and the first one where I finally managed to make absolutely no printing mistakes. That alone makes it special to me.

I also love St. Satosius Contra Draconem (2025), which is inspired by the classic depiction of Saint George fighting the dragon, reimagined through bitcoin mythology.

Works by ZETRA, RYR, and Cypherpunk Now, alongside other European artists, will be presented at Bitcoin Amsterdam, November 4–6, 2026, as part of the Bitcoin Museum & Art Gallery (BMAG) programming. Additional artworks and editions will be available through https://shop.museum.b.tc.

Explore more work by the featured artists at ZETRA, RYR, Cypherpunk Now, and www.martin-fischer.cz.

The Bitcoin Museum & Art Gallery (BMAG) organizes international exhibitions, auctions, and artist collaborations exploring bitcoin and its cultural implications. Learn more at museum.b.tc.

markets, Bloomberg reported.
London's trading industry is coming home!
The California-based
company raised
$150 million in an ...
content:
2026-10-14T17:53:27.213+02:00

Wednesday, 14/10/2026 | 15:53 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • The firm holds over $3.5 billion in US shares backing tokenised products from more than 10 issuers.
  • BitGo and Coinbase are expanding prime brokerage operations as crypto firms target institutional clients.

Alpaca plans to launch a prime brokerage business in the first quarter of financial year 2027 as it expands into services connecting cryptocurrency and traditional financial markets, Bloomberg reported.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The California-based company raised $150 million in an equity round in January, reaching a valuation of $1.15 billion. In August, Monetae launched 70 tokenised US stocks in El Salvador using Alpaca's brokerage infrastructure, extending its role in the tokenised equity market.

Prime Brokers Address Funding Gaps Across Markets

Chief Executive Officer Yoshi Yokokawa said the company aims to meet demand for financing and other services that help large investors manage positions across markets.

Speaking on the sidelines of the Token2049 conference in Singapore, he cited capital efficiency as a key reason for using prime brokers.

Prime brokers provide financing, custody and securities lending to hedge funds and other institutional investors. These services can help firms manage funding gaps between cryptocurrency platforms, which often require trades to be pre-funded, and traditional securities markets, where settlement takes longer.

Alpaca Holds $3.5 Billion in Tokenised Shares

Alpaca also provides custody for tokenised equities . Yokokawa said it holds more than $3.5 billion in underlying US shares backing tokenised products from more than 10 issuers, including Binance, Coinbase and Crypto.com. The value of these holdings has increased about eightfold over the past year.

The company is working to make tokenised stocks easier to convert into the underlying shares. Yokokawa said reliable conversion and redemption processes were needed before leverage could be expanded in these transactions.

“We have to solve this interoperability first, in terms of redemption and minting,” he said.

Alpaca is also exploring ways to offset obligations between trading firms, which could reduce the collateral required for individual transactions.

The prime brokerage launch will require additional financing capacity. Alpaca raised $135 million in equity and $300 million in debt earlier this year. Yokokawa said the company expects to fund the business through a combination of its balance sheet, debt and credit lines.

Other cryptocurrency firms are also expanding into prime brokerage. BitGo recently said it wanted the business to become its main revenue driver, while Coinbase has reported growth in its prime brokerage operations.

Chief Executive Officer Yoshi Yokokawa said the company aims to meet demand for financing and other services that help large investors manage positions across markets.

Speaking on the sidelines of the Token2049 conference in Singapore, he cited capital efficiency as a key reason for using prime brokers.

Prime brokers provide financing, custody and securities lending to hedge funds and other institutional investors. These services can help firms manage funding gaps between cryptocurrency platforms, which often require trades to be pre-funded, and traditional securities markets, where settlement takes longer.

Alpaca Holds $3.5 Billion in Tokenised Shares

Alpaca also provides custody for tokenised equities . Yokokawa said it holds more than $3.5 billion in underlying US shares backing tokenised products from more than 10 issuers, including Binance, Coinbase and Crypto.com. The value of these holdings has increased about eightfold over the past year.

The company is working to make tokenised stocks easier to convert into the underlying shares. Yokokawa said reliable conversion and redemption processes were needed before leverage could be expanded in these transactions.

“We have to solve this interoperability first, in terms of redemption and minting,” he said.

Alpaca is also exploring ways to offset obligations between trading firms, which could reduce the collateral required for individual transactions.

The prime brokerage launch will require additional financing capacity. Alpaca raised $135 million in equity and $300 million in debt earlier this year. Yokokawa said the company expects to fund the business through a combination of its balance sheet, debt and credit lines.

Other cryptocurrency firms are also expanding into prime brokerage. BitGo recently said it wanted the business to become its main revenue driver, while Coinbase has reported growth in its prime brokerage operations.

title: Ripple Taps DriveWealth to Bring RLUSD Settlement to 100+ Global Investing Partners
summary:
Key Takeaways: Ripple is in a partnership with DriveWealth, to secure the integration of the RLUSD settlement, cross-border payment capabilities, digital asset custody and institutional equity financing. With the initial
The post Ripple Taps DriveWealth to Bring RLUSD Settlement to 100+ Global Inves...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Ripple is in a partnership with DriveWealth, to secure the integration of the RLUSD settlement, cross-border payment capabilities, digital asset custody and institutional equity financing.
  • With the initial rollout of stablecoins set to begin in Europe, then the USA.
  • Ripple has a video conference with over 100 partners worldwide and will be introducing it to the DriveWealth platform.

DriveWealth, a brokerage infrastructure provider for fintechs and financial institutions across the globe. Announced on October 14, the agreement aims to connect traditional investing services with stablecoin settlement and blockchain-based payment rails.

  • RLUSD Targets Faster Brokerage Funding
  • RLUSD Gains Another Institutional Use Case
    • Four Areas of Financial Infrastructure
    • DriveWealth Network Could Extend Ripple’s Reach

RLUSD Targets Faster Brokerage Funding

The collaboration will initially involve Ripple’s stablecoin technology being used within DriveWealth’s settlement activities in Europe, potentially extending to the U.S. in the future. RLUSD will feature on the XRP Ledger (XRPL), along with the minting and burning capability of Ripple.

It aims to facilitate the transfer of assets into collateral accounts for the brokerage clients without doing anything but using wire transfers. With the proposed scheme, investors should be able to place trades with stablecoins that can be repatriated to cash very soon.

The firms are fixing a TIMING PROBLEM in financial markets. U.S. equities settle T+1 and international bank transfers can be longer. These delays can result in capital being held captive between deals and a need for extra liquidity.

Read More: Ripple Says $XRP, RLUSD Could Turn 24/7 Crypto Into a CFO Treasury Tool

RLUSD Gains Another Institutional Use Case

RLUSD is Ripple’s USD stablecoin, pegged to the price of the U.S. dollar. If it is integrated into DriveWealth’s infrastructure, it will provide a broader solution than just crypto trading, adding to the funding and settlement for conventional investment accounts.

The statement did not include any specifics regarding expected transactions or a launch date nor the exact date of U.S. expansion.

Four Areas of Financial Infrastructure

The agreement is not limited to settlement of stablecoins. By adding support for Ripple Payments, DriveWealth will make it easier to accept funds from its international partners for its global brokerage network.

European digital asset custody for DriveWealth is another focus for the companies, and other markets will be explored over time. DriveWealth and Ripple Prime separately are looking at equity financing programs in the Delta One business that covers U.S. equities and equity derivatives on which Ripple Prime operates.

These efforts are all designed to tie payments, custody, treasury and trading together. Additionally, DriveWealth has plans to place its treasury and custody platform on top of the Ripple network, providing clients with a more integrated approach to managing dollars, stablecoins and crypto assets.

DriveWealth Network Could Extend Ripple’s Reach

DriveWealth offers brokerage-as-a-service infrastructure for U.S.-market access to over 100 partners worldwide, including fintech, digital wallet and financial organizations.

That network gives Ripple a potential route to introduce its digital asset services into existing investment platforms rather than relying solely on direct crypto adoption. DriveWealth CEO Naureen Hassan said the company had already enabled 24/5 trading and now wanted funding capabilities that better match market access.

title: AI agents make 138 million crypto payments as U.S. dominates spending on AI models
summary: U.S.-linked wallets account for just over 88% of tracked AI model payments, dwarfing China’s 0.1% share, according to new Chainalysis research.
content:
Oct 14, 2026, 11:35 a.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

  • AI agents made more than 138 million transactions through Coinbase’s x402 protocol, using cryptocurrency to buy data, computing power and access to AI models.
  • U.S.-linked wallets accounted for 88.1% of identified payments for AI model inference, while Chinese-linked wallets dominated payments for security and code-analysis services.
  • More than 87% of analyzed x402 payments were worth 10 cents or less, underscoring stablecoins’ potential for micropayments while leaving questions about genuine commercial demand.

Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are no longer just talking to each other. They are paying for services, buying data and even purchasing access to tokens the AI models, with more than 138 million transactions recorded through the x402 protocol on Coinbase’s Base blockchain, according to a Chainalysis’ Inside North America's $3 trillion crypto economy: Agentic commerce accelerates report.

The United States dominates this emerging market. U.S.linked wallets accounted for 88.1% of the geographically identified payments for AI model inference, compared with just 0.1% for Chinese-linked wallets, the blockchain analytics firm found.

"One possible explanation is that Chinese developers are more inclined to use open-weight models such as DeepSeek and Qwen, reducing their need to purchase metered inference services," Eric Jardine, Chainalysis' head of research, told CoinDesk.

The findings, released Wednesday, come as Visa, Mastercard, Stripe and other payments giants have backed the x402 protocol, while Coinbase has begun allowing business customers to accept payments from AI agents.

Yat Siu, co-founder and chairman of Animoca Brands, recently told CoinDesk that over the next few years he estimates up to 100 billion AI agents will be transacting on the internet and they will be using crypto. And crypto’s next billion users might be AI agents paying with stablecoins. “Stablecoins are particularly well suited to the kinds of transactions we expect AI agents to make at first,” Stephanie Cohen, Cloudflare’s chief strategy officer, told CoinDesk.

Unlike traditional card payments, stablecoins can handle transactions worth fractions of a cent, allowing AI agents to buy data, computing power and other services without human intervention. The new Chainalysis figures offer evidence of growing use of those payment systems, although transaction counts alone do not establish how much represents genuine commercial demand.

Much of the activity runs through x402, a payments protocol incubated by Coinbase that allows AI agents to pay automatically for digital services using crypto.

More than 87% of x402 payments analyzed by Chainalysis were worth between one-hundredth of a cent and 10 cents, making them too small to process economically through traditional credit card networks.

The amounts remain small. In July, x402 processed roughly 75 million payments worth just $24 million over 30 days. Earlier research also raised questions about artificial activity on the network.

Among wallets first funded in the second quarter of 2026, 89.3% received additional funding within 30 days, compared with 70.6% for wallets first funded in the Q3 2025. The analysis excluded wallets that made payments on one only one day.

The time between a wallet receiving funds and making its first x40 payment also fell sharply, from an average of 73 days in late 2025 to just 18 minutes in Q3 2026.

China, meanwhile, showed a different pattern of activity. Chinese-linked wallets accounted for roughly 90% of geographically identified payments for security and code-analysis services, much of it directed toward AgentLisa, an AI-powered smart contract auditing platform.

He cautioned against interpreting that gap as evidence that open-source AI was undermining Asia's payments market.

"That's one possible interpretation, but we wouldn't go so far as to say open-source AI is starving Asia's on-chain inference market," he said.

The figures measure identifiable transactions through x402, rather than the entire global market for AI payments.

"AI agents are becoming economic actors where every agent is effectively a new 'user' of the blockchain," Tejwani said in the report.

For now, the transactions remain small, but Chainalysis' findings suggest autonomous software is beginning to establish its own spending habits, with the United States leading the market for paid AI services.

title: Crypto Long & Short: Why gold and bitcoin belong in the same portfolio
content:
Oct 14, 2026, 11:05 a.m. EDT

5 min read

Summary

You're reading Crypto Long & Short, our weekly newsletter featuring insights, news and analysis for the professional investor. Sign up here to get it in your inbox every Wednesday.

Note: The views expressed in this column are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect those of CoinDesk, Inc., CoinDesk Indices or its owners and affiliates.

Happy Wednesday,

This is your institutional newsletter, Crypto Long & Short. This week:

  • Steve Neamtz of Yorkville America on what gold has that bitcoin is still building
  • Top headlines institutions should pay attention to by Francisco Rodrigues
  • “CHIP rebounds as USD.AI pivots to a loan factory” in Chart of the Week

…and if you’re looking for bitcoin meets Broadway: Crypto is taking the stage in New York City. “Bitcoin Bad Boy,” a comedy by Ben Schiller, runs Oct. 15-25 at the Chain Theatre. The show centers around a family in debt, a coder who wants to build a better world and a memecoin. Learn more.

Thanks for joining us!

- Kim Klemballa

Gold and bitcoin are allies against debasement

by Steve Neamtz, CEO, Yorkville America

Gold trading near $4,200 an ounce alongside bitcoin BTC$81,499.86 holding around $84,000 has revived a familiar argument: Should investors own gold or the “digital gold” alternative?

For 5,000 years, gold has demonstrated its value as a reserve asset. Bitcoin’s 17-year history offers far less empirical evidence. But the supply of both assets cannot be expanded by central bank or fiscal policymakers. Their shared scarcity thus takes on greater significance in a world awash in debt.

In the United States alone, the federal debt has climbed past $39 trillion. The U.S. now spends roughly $1 trillion a year simply servicing its existing debt, and the outlook is even more challenging for much of the developed world. Currencies often serve as the relief valve for fiscal concerns. The U.S. dollar, for example, has lost roughly 40% of its purchasing power over the past two decades.

Against this backdrop, it is important to understand where we believe supply-constrained assets fit within long-term diversified portfolios. A 2025 study in Resources Policy, using multifractal cross-correlation analysis across six asset classes — developed and emerging equities, bonds, commodities, energy and crypto — found that “neither gold nor bitcoin can be classified as a hedge or safe haven for financial markets” under rigorous testing.

That’s a finding about market-drawdown behavior — whether either asset reliably moves against stocks and bonds when markets fall. It says nothing about whether either holds value relative to a currency that is slowly, but steadily, depreciating against them. Investors and allocators buying gold or bitcoin often aren’t using them as shock absorbers. They’re making a debasement bet: that an asset independent of any government’s promise to pay provides diversification benefits.

On that bet, gold and bitcoin aren’t racing against each other — they’re at different points on the same course. Gold already has the custody, legal and reserve-eligibility infrastructure that lets central banks act on a debasement and reserve-currency diversification thesis today. Bitcoin doesn’t yet — at least not fully.

Gold’s lead reflects decades of built plumbing, not a stronger claim to the thesis. Bitcoin does not have the same penetration in terms of knowledge. It is earlier on the same curve, not a different one, and it often appeals to a younger generation of investors.

Central banks bought a record 289 metric tons of gold in the second quarter of 2026, after 244 metric tons in the first, according to data from an industry body funded by mining interests. This is worth flagging even as the pace of buying is independently corroborated elsewhere, and the clearest signal of where reserve managers are putting money and why. Bitcoin is being bought into the same thesis through a newer wrapper: spot ETFs, which solve the custody problem but not the sovereign-reserve status central banks need.

None of this requires picking a side. Central banks are buying gold on infrastructure that already exists; institutions are buying bitcoin on infrastructure still being built — the same debasement logic, two different stages. Financial media has already started calling it one trade, not two competing ones, as coverage of the “debasement trade” picked up through 2026. The right question for 2027 isn’t which asset wins. It’s how much of each diversifier belongs in a portfolio built for eroding purchasing power. The volatility is very different between gold and bitcoin, and we believe solutions that help investors with sizing these two anti-debasement assets will add value to portfolio construction efforts.

Gold and bitcoin can experience substantial price declines and may fail to preserve purchasing power. Bitcoin is highly speculative and subject to significant volatility. Diversification does not ensure profit or protect against loss. Investment products providing exposure to these assets involve additional fees and risks.

Headlines of the week

by Francisco Rodrigues

This week’s headlines show institutional crypto expanding through bank trading, regulated custody and national ETF access, while European regulators moved to force unauthorized stablecoins off trading platforms.

  • EU gives crypto platforms three months to remove unauthorized stablecoins: The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) told authorized platforms to block new trading and purchases of stablecoins that do not comply with the Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation (MiCA), with national regulators expected to resolve existing customer holdings within three months.
  • Russia’s largest bank secures approval to trade crypto: Sberbank joined the country’s crypto exchange register and plans to open trading to all clients on Dec. 1, with bitcoin, ether and tether already being tested in its app.
  • Ledger says spy chip in resold devices stole wallet recovery phrases: A covert implant in signers sold by reseller CryptoBilis read recovery phrases from device screens and sent them over a mobile network, with onchain researchers estimating up to $93.2 million lost across more than 300 wallets.
  • Thailand opens its stock exchange to locally listed bitcoin and ether ETFs: Rules taking effect Oct. 16 will let domestic asset managers launch single-asset crypto funds, provided at least 80% of their net assets track bitcoin or ether and regulated custodians hold the tokens.
  • Standard Chartered launches institutional RLUSD custody in Dubai: The bank now holds Ripple’s stablecoin for eligible clients and plans to connect those holdings to LMAX so they can serve as trading collateral without leaving the bank, subject to approvals and testing.

Chart of the week

CHIP rebounds as USD.AI pivots to a loan factory

USD.AI active loans dropped ~22% to ~$311 million on Oct. 2 and have been flat since, while CHIP has rebounded ~35% since Oct. 1 to ~5.8 cents (still ~48% below its April high). The catalyst is GLX, a loan-factory model (originate, sell performing loans to institutions, recycle the capital), which could drive a rebound in active loans by recycling capital into new loans without a much bigger balance sheet.

title: Ethereum (ETH) Price Prediction: ETH Holds Near $2,500 as ETF Flows Turn Positive and Long Positions Reach Four-Year High
summary: Ethereum holds near $2,500 as ETF flows turn positive and longs hit a four-year high, with traders watching $2,600 for a breakout toward $3,000.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: ETH

Ethereum holds near $2,500 as ETF flows turn positive and longs hit a four-year high, with traders watching $2,600 for a breakout toward $3,000.

Ethereum is holding close to $2,500 after a volatile start to October, with the market now showing a mixture of improving institutional flows and elevated derivatives positioning. According to Brave New Coin, ETH is trading around $2,511.53, up 0.08% over the past 24 hours, after spending much of the session between roughly $2,490 and $2,530.

Ethereum Fractal Pointing Toward $4,600

Ethereum’s latest structure is beginning to resemble the setup that preceded last year’s larger advance. In 2025, ETH spent several weeks consolidating around the mid-$2,000 region before a sharp downside sweep briefly pushed price below support. That move was quickly reversed, and the reclaim eventually developed into a much stronger trend.

Famous crypto analyst Ash Crypto is highlighting a similar sequence in the current market. ETH has returned toward the $2,400-$2,300 region after the latest decline, placing the focus on whether buyers can recover and maintain this zone. If price stabilizes here, the recent selloff could begin to look more like a liquidity sweep than a sustained breakdown.

Ethereum’s current structure resembles the consolidation and downside sweep that preceded the larger 2025 expansion. Source: Ash Crypto via X.

The earlier cycle also shows that the recovery did not move straight toward the highs. ETH price first pushed through $3,000, then spent time consolidating in the mid, $3,000s before extending toward roughly $4,800. A similar progression in 2026 would bring the $4,600-$4,800 region back into focus, but only if the current support structure holds.

For now, the comparison remains conditional, not predictive. A sustained recovery above $2,400-$2,500 would strengthen the fractal and shift attention toward $3,000 as the next major step, while another breakdown below the recent low would weaken the setup and suggest that Ethereum still needs to establish a firmer base first.

Bitfinex Longs Reach Four-Year High

Ethereum Bitfinex bulls are ramping up their positioning for a potential major breakout. Data shared by Crypto Rover shows ETH long positions surging to their highest level in four years, with exposure rising sharply while price remains around the $2,500 region.

The buildup points to strong bullish conviction beneath the current market structure. Rather than waiting for Ethereum price to confirm a breakout first, smart money appears to be building long exposure during the consolidation, suggesting expectations of a much larger move once price begins clearing resistance.

The scale of the increase is also important. Long positioning has accelerated well beyond the levels seen during previous periods, showing that traders are committing more aggressively to the upside scenario. If ETH continues holding the $2,400-$2,500 base, this positioning could add further momentum to the next breakout attempt.

Ethereum long positions have reached their highest level in four years while price continues to trade near the $2,500 region. Source: Crypto Rover via X

Ethereum Sees $24.84M in ETF Inflows

Institutional flows have finally shown some improvement after a difficult stretch for Ethereum ETFs. U.S. spot ETH products recorded approximately $24.84 million in net inflows on October 13, marking the first positive session after 10 consecutive trading days of outflows.

Ethereum ETFs returned to net inflows with approximately $24.84 million on October 13 after 10 consecutive sessions of withdrawals. Source: Trader T via X

Trader T’s data shows Grayscale’s mini Ethereum ETF accounting for approximately $16.73 million of the daily inflow, while Fidelity’s FETH added another $8.11 million. The shift is notable after the previous session recorded roughly $85.43 million in net outflows and the five-day total had fallen to around $576.9 million in withdrawals.

If ETH ETF demand continues to recover while ETH holds above $2,500, institutional flows could begin providing a more supportive backdrop for the next rebound attempt.

Contrary: Whale Positioning Remains Cautious Below $2,600

Not all positioning data supports the bullish side yet. Ethereum’s Whale vs Retail Delta remains below zero, indicating that larger traders continue to carry greater short exposure than retail participants.

The imbalance has nevertheless improved. Data shared by CW8900 shows the delta recovering from much more negative levels recorded through September, while whale short positioning has also declined. That suggests larger traders are reducing some defensive exposure even though they have not yet shifted decisively bullish.

This distinction helps explain why ETH price remains stuck around $2,500 despite improving ETF flows and aggressive long positioning elsewhere in the market. A further recovery in the whale-retail delta, particularly alongside a move through $2,550-$2,600, would provide stronger evidence that larger participants are becoming more comfortable with the rebound.

Ethereum’s whale-versus-retail delta remains negative, although the gap has narrowed as whale short exposure declines. Source: CW8900 via X.

Ethereum Price Prediction: $2,600 Reclaim Could Reopen $3,000

Ethereum’s near-term price prediction is becoming easier to define after the latest volatility. The $2,400-$2,500 region has developed into the main base, while $2,600 remains the level buyers need to recover before the rebound can expand into a broader trend move.

A reclaim of $2,600 would improve the technical picture considerably and bring $2,700 back into focus. From there, the larger $3,000 level becomes more relevant, particularly if the historical fractal continues to hold and spot demand improves alongside the move.

The downside case is more straightforward. If ETH loses $2,400 and fails to recover the level quickly, the current base would begin to weaken, and the market could be forced into a deeper reset before another larger recovery develops.

What Traders Should Watch Next

The real question now is whether improving positioning can finally translate into Ethereum price strength. ETH longs are at a four-year high, ETF flows have returned to positive territory, and whale short exposure has started to ease, creating a noticeably stronger backdrop than earlier in the correction.

Ethereum price is trading at around $2,511, up 0.08% in the last 24 hours. Source: Brave New Coin

What traders need next is follow-through. A breakout supported by stronger spot demand and continued institutional inflows would carry more weight than another short-lived bounce, while renewed ETF selling or a return of aggressive whale shorts would weaken the recovery narrative. The next few sessions should therefore show whether the improvement beneath the surface is beginning to reach the chart.
