title: Gold Price Analysis: XAU/USD Eyes Recovery Toward $4,200 Resistance
summary: Gold has come back from the 2026 highs to about $4,156 per ounce, where a vital support zone is now coming into view.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: XAU

Gold has come back from the 2026 highs to about $4,156 per ounce, where a vital support zone is now coming into view.

One analyst considers the break below $4,140 as a nullification of the bullish setup but believes that $4,150-$4,160 is a potential area of interest for buyers. The weekly chart also indicates that money flow has turned negative, and traders will be interested to see if a buying defense can be sustained or if selling pressure will continue the pullback.

Gold Price Tests Support Between $4,150 and $4,160

After retesting its 2026 highs, gold is coming into a sweet spot, as traders monitor if buyers will go on the defensive at $4,150. An analyst on X noted that the 4150-4160 level could be a good top entry point for a bull run, while the area below $4140 would be a negative sign.

The analyst’s posting on October 13th does not spell a definite reversal but a trading plan, contingent upon a few conditions. Traders may consider going long if gold is trading above the recognized support level. But a drop below $4,140 would be a red flag to put the “buy” mentality on hold.

A possible recovery towards resistance at $4,200 is indicated on the accompanying chart. It also shows a slight dip followed by a bounce up, indicating that the analyst believes gold will retest support levels and then bounce back upward. Source: Cali Via X

The forecast is based on the price action in the vicinity of the entry area. If the price of gold stays above $4,150, the proposed scenario would be supported, but continued selling could bring the precious metal down.

The analyst also mentions some potential profit targets in the accompanying post, which are 100, 300, and 500 points. These are not targets but possibilities, and the situation relies on support to hold up.

Gold Price Chart Shows Pullback From 2026 High

A technical chart from TradingView displays Gold Spot’s weekly time frame against the U.S. dollar (XAU/USD). The displayed price is $4,156.005, down $38.640, or 0.92%, in the October 13, 2026 chart.

The longer-term chart indicates that gold has been moving higher since 2024 and 2025 and then sparked a rapid uptrend in 2026. The metal rallied to a new high before prices started to head back from the top. Source: TradingView

Gold has ceased its recent trend of rising, but it is still above its previous historical trading range. The chart depicts that the price broke out from a steep move and is now coming back, not continuing to follow an upward trend.

The new reading positions gold in the $4150–$4160 range that is highlighted in the X analysis. This overlap makes the zone worth considering, but the weekly TradingView chart does not necessarily validate the shorter time frame entry point indicated in the analyst’s post.

The two charts are also on different time frames.

The X post is about a short-term trading space, and TradingView displays the price history for gold over a longer time frame. Therefore, the suggested correction to $4200 must be considered a short-term scenario and not as a viable trend reversal.

Gold Price Momentum Declines as Money Flow Becomes Negative

The Chaikin Money Flow indicator (CMF) is part of the TradingView chart and is used to evaluate buying and selling pressure based on price and volume. It shows a reading of -0.02, which is only below the neutral level of zero.

When the CMF indicator has a negative reading, money is flowing out of the market instead of into the market during the period of time that the indicator measures. But it is near zero and not strong enough to confirm bearish selling pressure.

There is also an indication of increased trading during portions of the massive surge and subsequent pullback in gold. The recent pullback follows a significant range of activity, and traders will be eager to see whether the market holds up, so volatility could increase ahead.

The short-term forecast is for the $4150–$4160 range, as this is the next zone to monitor. Buyers have to defend it, and gold may try to reverse back to the $4,200 resistance level, which is shown in the X chart. A trend-confirming move in that area would give some more validation of a turnaround, though the chart doesn’t suggest that this will happen.

The negative side of the picture is that a decline below $4,140 will jeopardize the bullish outlook of the analyst. Traders would then have to evaluate if gold will find a bottom at the current price.

As a whole, the X time frame is in a buying situation, and the weekly chart of gold is correcting from a strong bull market run. The price of $4,140 in XAU/USD could be a key level to see if the current pullback reaches a bottom or continues.

title: EasyA hits $1.1 billion valuation, targets 2027 public listing and tokenized shares
summary: The blockchain and AI developer platform has completed two years of audits and wants its shares available onchain from the first day of trading.
content:
Updated Oct 14, 2026, 12:05 p.m. EDTPublished Oct 14, 2026, 10:49 a.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • EasyA, a platform for building blockchain and artificial intelligence applications, received an independent valuation of $1.1 billion as it prepares for a direct listing in the first half of next year.
  • The company has submitted a draft registration to the Securities and Exchange Commission, though its valuation does not guarantee the price investors will pay once its shares begin trading.
  • EasyA, which says its app has more than 1.3 million users, is considering offering tokenized shares and is expanding into tokenization projects and applications involving AI agents.

EasyA, a platform that helps developers build blockchain and artificial intelligence applications, reached a $1.1 billion valuation as it prepares to go public in the first half of next year, co-founder and CEO Philip Kwok told CoinDesk in an interview Tuesday.

The platform, which was founded by brothers Philip and Dominic Kwok, plans to pursue a direct public listing, which would allow its existing shareholders to sell their stock publicly without the company raising fresh capital through a traditional initial public offering (IPO).

EasyA has already submitted a draft registration to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The company has completed two years of audits by the accounting firm PKF and received an independent valuation based on its financial performance and growth prospects. The valuation does not necessarily indicate what investors will pay for EasyA once its shares begin trading.

The planned listing would give public-market investors access to a business that helps blockchain networks and AI companies attract developers and build applications. It would also test investor appetite for companies that sell the infrastructure and services behind those industries, rather than for cryptocurrencies or AI models themselves.

"Given we are going public, and we're going public via a direct listing, that means that we of course need to have an independent valuation," Phil Kwok said. He explained that the $1.1 billion figure was determined by a third party using audited financial statements, operating performance, growth plans and comparisons with publicly traded companies.

EasyA says its app has more than 1.3 million users, ranging from software developers to people using AI tools to create applications. It works with companies including Ripple and Solana,, helping them introduce their technology to developers through educational programs and hackathons.

The company also wants its shares to be available in tokenized form, potentially from the first day of public trading.

"That's definitely on the roadmap," Dominic Kwok, EasyA's co-founder and chief operating officer, said of the tokenization plans.

Tokenized equities are gaining attention from major financial firms. Robinhood built a blockchain for tokenized stocks, while analysts expect the SEC's work on tokenized securities to open opportunities for brokers, custodians and blockchain infrastructure providers. Apia, Samoa, October 14, 2026 – The crypto market saw a notable rally in the just-concluded third quarter. It was also the quarter in which HTX turned 13. Over the past 13 years, the industry has weathered multiple bull and bear cycles, and HTX has stood alongside users worldwide throughout them. Resilience in navigating market cycles has been a defining characteristic of HTX over the past 13 years.

To mark its anniversary themed “Resilience Reveals the Future”, HTX launched the 13th-Anniversary Carnival and Trading Championship #3, among other celebratory events, in the third quarter, celebrating alongside users worldwide. Meanwhile, the platform continued to invest in TradFi, trending assets, yield products, and global compliance, delivering an outstanding quarterly performance report.

13th-Anniversary Celebrations Conclude, with Participation from Users Worldwide

On August 13, HTX kicked off its 13th-anniversary celebrations with the Anniversary Carnival. Its spot, futures, Earn and lending businesses rolled out exclusive anniversary promotions in succession, launching a celebration that lasted more than a month.

The annual trading competition Trading Championship #3 was the centerpiece of the anniversary celebrations. It attracted 45,000 registrations and generated 6.8 billion USDT in futures trading volume, making it the platform’s largest campaign of the quarter by both participation and trading volume. Meanwhile, HTX futures copy trading volume grew 21% quarter over quarter.

For spot trading, a series of 13th-anniversary campaigns, including the Individual Challenge, Trending Cryptos Margin Trading Carnival, and Points Tasks, played a key role in driving spot trading growth during the quarter. Over the three-month period, HTX launched 14 themed spot trading campaigns, attracting more than 46,000 registrations and generating over 500 million USDT in trading volume across the campaigns.

For 13 years, HTX and users worldwide have navigated one market cycle after another together. The anniversary celebrations were both a gesture of appreciation for users’ long-term support and a reflection of HTX’s determination to carry its resilience into the next 13 years.

TradFi Asset Offerings Expand as Quarterly Trading Volume More Than Doubles

In the third quarter, HTX listed 183 new futures assets, including 154 stocks and index-related assets. As of now, the platform offers 278 tradable stock assets, spanning US stocks, major global indices and ETFs, pre-IPO unicorns, and leading companies in Japan and South Korea, continuing to lead the industry in multi-market stock asset coverage.

HTX’s asset lineup focuses on four key sectors: AI hardware and semiconductor computing power, global e-commerce and internet companies, leading Asia-Pacific companies and major indices, and high-dividend blue-chip stocks. AI and semiconductor computing, leading Asia-Pacific companies, and pre-IPO unicorns were key themes throughout the quarter. Popular assets such as POLYMARKET, OURA and MOONSHOT were also listed. Eligible users can access global market opportunities through HTX without switching between platforms. This service is not available in jurisdictions subject to regulatory restrictions.

The expanded asset lineup drove rapid growth in trading volume. So far the cumulative TradFi trading volume on HTX has approached $6 billion, with $4.1 billion generated in the third quarter alone, more than doubling the cumulative total from the previous quarter.

The trading experience was upgraded alongside these developments. Stock perpetual futures feature a dividend settlement mechanism, allowing position values to adjust more continuously when an underlying stock goes ex-dividend and reducing the impact of non-trading-related price adjustments on users’ positions. TradFi asset detail pages include market data, news updates, and company profile, bringing key information together in one place. Dedicated categories for stocks, commodities and ETFs have also been added to market rankings, making it easier for users to discover assets. HTX has also upgraded its TradFi trading fee structure, bringing its net trading fees into the industry’s top tier.

HTX is also taking a longer-term view of the convergence of traditional finance and crypto markets. As real-world assets (RWAs), particularly tokenized stocks, become an increasingly important area of development in the global digital asset industry, the platform is monitoring regulatory developments and exploring regulatory frameworks and compliance pathways in preparation for future product innovation. All related products and services offered by the platform operate within the framework of applicable laws and regulations, and access restrictions are applied to users in certain jurisdictions as required.

Trending Assets Emerge as Earn and Lending Products Put Funds to Work Efficiently

In the third quarter, HTX listed new projects attracting strong market interest, several of which were first listed on the platform. Niulai was the quarter’s top-performing newly listed token, recording a peak gain of more than 500%. DOS and STONK each recorded peak gains of 240% after listing.

Earn and lending products expanded alongside new asset listings. During the quarter, HTX Earn changed the launch schedule for its new-token products from weekly updates to real-time synchronization with new listings, allowing users to access corresponding Earn products as soon as eligible popular tokens become available. Nearly 500,000 users participated in HTX Earn during the quarter, with subscription amounts totaling nearly 1 billion USDT. SVIP Flexible Earn products added BTC and ETH, expanding the options available to users with large holdings. In addition, SmartEarn introduced a trading-linked APY boost, offering a base APY of 4% upon activation and up to 9% APY for users who meet the required trading volume threshold. This further expands the yield potential for idle assets.

Margin and Convert features added 21 tradable assets, with XAUT becoming the first precious metal asset available through Convert. This further expanded the range of assets available for trading, borrowing and use as collateral. Loan interest rates are adjusted frequently in response to market conditions across more than 50 cryptocurrencies. Interest rates for large loans remain among the lower levels in the industry.

Risk management tools were also upgraded. Trailing stop orders and MMR TP/SL orders were launched successively. Stop-loss levels can automatically track market movements, giving users with large positions and high leverage greater flexibility in managing risk.

Advancing Global Compliance and Making a Major Brand Appearance at TOKEN2049

Compliance is a prerequisite for global expansion. In the third quarter, HTX made further progress on compliance initiatives in several key markets. In Dubai, the establishment of the relevant applicant entity received preliminary approval from the Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (VARA), with subsequent regulatory applications and compliance reviews proceeding as planned. In Pakistan, following the formal publication of virtual asset service regulations and the launch of a licensing application process, HTX continued to advance the establishment of its local entity, its formal license application, and the development of its compliance framework, building on the No Objection Certificate (NoC) already obtained from the Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (PVARA).

HTX continued to strengthen its presence in regional markets. In August, HTX Ventures participated in Conviction Vietnam, building connections with local users and Web3 ecosystem partners. As the fourth quarter began, HTX appeared at TOKEN2049, a major annual gathering for the global crypto industry. Held in Singapore from October 7–8, the event brought together projects, investment firms, developers, and industry builders from around the world. HTX Ventures exhibited at the Sands Expo and Convention Centre in Singapore, engaging invited guests through brand displays and on-site interactions. Justin Sun, adviser to HTX and a core supporter of HTX DAO, attended related events and delivered a speech. He visited the HTX Ventures booth to meet with the team and other industry participants.

At Future Night, a private, invitation-only event hosted by HTX DAO during the same period, Justin Sun shared his views on industry trends via video. He noted that the crypto industry is becoming more closely connected with traditional finance. AI is changing how wealth is created, while crypto and digital finance are transforming how wealth is held and transferred. He also said that stablecoins could play a greater role in global payments and settlement, while the on-chain adoption of traditional assets such as bonds, funds and gold is likely to continue developing. The free flow of value in the digital world, he said, will be an important trend to watch over the next decade.

During the event, HTX DAO also hosted a private VIP dinner. Justin Sun met face to face with industry representatives, ecosystem contributors, and partners to exchange views on industry developments, market changes, product experiences, and future collaboration.

HTX DAO Ecosystem Expands as Q3 $HTX Burn Approaches

HTX DAO continued to support the long-term value of $HTX in the third quarter by steadily implementing its deflationary mechanism through quarterly token burns, while expanding $HTX use cases and building consensus among developers and the community. These efforts aim to lay a solid foundation for the ecosystem’s long-term development.

On July 15, HTX DAO completed its Q2 2026 $HTX token burn, valued at more than $13.6 million, bringing cumulative burns and donations to 117.79 trillion tokens. In line with its quarterly burn schedule, the Q3 $HTX token burn is scheduled to take place on October 15.

On the ecosystem front, HTX DAO focused on developers and the community. The Genesis Hackathon, co-hosted by HTX DAO and B.AI, attracted more than 200 developer teams exploring $HTX use cases, AI agent finance, on-chain asset management, and DAO tools. At Future Night, HTX DAO ambassador Molly shared that several projects developed by global university teams participating in the hackathon had advanced to further incubation stages and were exploring ways to integrate with use cases across the $HTX ecosystem.

Molly also shared that nearly 200 active volunteers were independently contributing to HTX DAO community development. In the fourth quarter, HTX DAO plans to develop regional community nodes to support members in organizing events and exchanging ideas.  She also noted that HTX, as an ecosystem participant, continues to optimize withdrawal fees, gather user feedback, and improve the app experience.

Navigating Market Cycles with Resilience, Shaping the Future Together with Users Worldwide

Thirteen years ago, HTX began as a digital asset trading platform. Today, it has grown into a comprehensive blockchain ecosystem serving users worldwide. Over the years, markets have experienced both highs and lows, and the industry landscape has evolved. Throughout these changes, HTX has remained committed to putting users first. Regardless of market conditions, improving its products and prioritizing the security of user assets remain among the platform’s top priorities.

Standing at the beginning of its 14th year, HTX will continue to navigate market cycles with resilience and build the future together with users worldwide.

Founded in 2013, HTX has evolved from a virtual asset exchange into a comprehensive ecosystem of blockchain businesses that span digital asset trading, derivatives, research, investments, incubation, and other businesses.

Guided by its vision to “Achieve Financial Freedom for 8 Billion People Worldwide,” HTX works to make the digital asset space more accessible to a broader audience. The platform continues to develop its products and services in response to user needs and an evolving industry landscape.

title: BlackRock's crypto ETF assets surge 63% but remain far below 2025 peak
summary: The asset manager's crypto assets surged 63% to $79.6 billion as investors returned, but holdings remain 23% below year-ago levels.
content:
Buod

  • BlackRock said its digital asset funds attracted $7.9 billion in third-quarter inflows, reversing roughly $2.2 billion in outflows during the first half of 2026.
  • Rising crypto prices accounted for $22.9 billion of the $30.8 billion increase in assets under management during the quarter.
  • Despite the rebound, BlackRock's digital asset holdings remain 23% below year-ago levels, even as investors added $6.3 billion over the past 12 months.

BlackRock's crypto funds had a much better third quarter than first half of the year but they still have a long way to go to recover the assets lost during the broader crypto market downturn.

The asset manager reported $79.6 billion in digital assets under management at the end of September, a 63% jump from $48.8 billion at the end of June, according to its third-quarter earnings report released Wednesday.

Investors added $7.9 billion to BlackRock's digital asset products during the quarter, more than making up for the roughly $2.2 billion they withdrew during the first six months of 2026.

The reversal came as crypto markets recovered from a slump earlier this year. Bitcoin BTC$81,499.86 and other cryptocurrencies had faced pressure during the first half of the year, weighing on the value of funds that hold them. The third-quarter recovery gave those funds a lift, while renewed investor demand added to their assets.

Rising crypto prices did most of the heavy lifting. Of the $30.8 billion BlackRock added in digital assets during the quarter, $22.9 billion came from market gains, while investors contributed another $7.9 billion.

Even after the rebound, BlackRock's crypto holdings remain 23% below the nearly $104 billion it managed a year ago.

That gap isn't the result of investors abandoning its products. Over the past 12 months, BlackRock's digital asset funds attracted $6.3 billion in net new money. But declines in the market value of those assets erased $30.6 billion over the same period.

The figures offer a reminder of how much BlackRock's crypto business depends on the price of the assets its funds hold, even as investors continue to put money into them.

BlackRock, which operates the iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), earned $39 million in quarterly fees and securities lending revenue from its digital asset products.

The asset manager did not provide separate asset or flow figures for its bitcoin fund in the earnings release.

title: Bitcoin Slips Below $83,000 After Hotter-Than-Expected US Inflation Data
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Slips Below $83,000 After Hotter-Than-Expected US Inflation Data
The price of bitcoin slid Wednesday after data dropped showing that U.S. consumer prices shot up more than expected in September due to rising gasoline prices.  The biggest cryptocurrency by market cap was rec...
content:
The price of bitcoin slid Wednesday after data dropped showing that U.S. consumer prices shot up more than expected in September due to rising gasoline prices. 

The biggest cryptocurrency by market cap was recently trading for close to $82,827 after dropping nearly 1% over a 24-hour period. At one point on Wednesday morning in New York, bitcoin fell as low as nearly $82,331. 

Over the past seven days, the coin has dropped by more than 1%. Bitcoin’s price had its best quarter in years after rallying in August and September and leading many analysts to declare it to have exited a bear market. 

But sticky inflation is still weighing — in the short-term — on the cryptocurrency. 

Data Wednesday showed that the Consumer Price Index rose 0.6% in September after climbing 0.4% in August. 

In the 12 months through September, the CPI advanced 3.7% after rising 3.4% in August, the Labor Department’s Bureau of Labor Statistics said. 

High prices in the U.S., in part spurred by the Trump Administration’s decision to attack Iran with Israel this year, have led the Federal Reserve to hint it may keep interest rates higher for longer. 

The central bank in September said getting inflation down was its number one priority and hiked rates. 

Bitcoin’s price has been sensitive to interest rate hikes in the past because higher borrowing costs restrict the liquidity the digital coin needs to run — along with other “risk-on” assets like stocks. 

Still, the price of bitcoin rose in September despite the Federal Reserve talking tough on inflation.  

The central bank will reveal what it plans to do with interest rates on October 28. As of Wednesday, fed funds futures were pricing a 47% chance of a rate hike at the Fed’s October meeting, according to CME Group’s FedWatch tool.

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Former FTX Europe chief targets U.S. tokenized stock trading with new SEC exemption
summary: Nasdaq-listed Perpetuals.com is the second company to pursue a U.S. tokenized stock marketplace under the SEC's new framework, following a joint venture between OKX and NYSE parent ICE.
content:
Skip to main content

  • Crypto News

Oct 14, 2026, 10:08 a.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

  • Nasdaq-listed Perpetuals.com plans to offer tokenized U.S. stocks under the SEC's new innovation exemption, following an earlier proposal from an OKX–ICE joint venture.
  • CEO Patrick Gruhn co-founded Digital Assets AG, which developed stock-linked tokens for crypto exchanges including Binance and FTX before being acquired by FTX Group.
  • Trading could begin in mid-November at the earliest, though the company still needs to complete technical and compliance preparations before launch.

A Nasdaq-listed fintech company led by a former FTX Europe executive is planning to bring tokenized U.S. stocks trading onto blockchain rails under the Securities and Exchange Commission's (SEC) new regulatory framework.

Perpetuals.com (PDC), headed by CEO Patrick Gruhn, filed a notice on Wednesday that it plans to operate a tokenized securities venue under the SEC's five-year "innovation exemption," which allows certain marketplaces to trade U.S. stocks on public blockchains without registering as traditional securities exchanges.

The move makes Perpetuals.com the second company to pursue a marketplace under the exemption, following OKXICE, a joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), which last week filed plans for round-the-clock trading of more than 60 tokenized U.S. stocks.

The exemption, introduced in September, allows certain marketplaces to trade U.S. stocks on public blockchains without registering as traditional securities exchanges. It requires tokens to carry the same shareholder rights as ordinary shares, including dividends and voting rights, while giving companies 30 days to object to having their shares traded on a tokenized securities venue.

A return to tokenized stocks

The move marks a return to tokenized equities for Gruhn and his team, who helped develop some of the earliest stock-linked tokens offered by crypto exchanges including Binance and FTX in 2021.

Gruhn co-founded Digital Assets AG, a Swiss-based tokenization company that worked with German investment firm CM-Equity to bring digital tokens linked to stocks such as Tesla and Coinbase to crypto traders. Digital Assets AG was later acquired by FTX Group, becoming part of FTX Europe, which Gruhn led before the crypto exchange group's collapse in November 2022.

Those early products differed from the securities envisioned under the SEC's new framework. While they offered price exposure to underlying shares, Binance's stock tokens did not provide voting rights. Binance discontinued the offering in July 2021 amid regulatory scrutiny, including concerns raised by German regulator BaFin over the lack of a published securities prospectus.

"The Perpetuals team has long been trailblazers in tokenization, and this expansion into the U.S. allows us to further utilize our platform and deep expertise," Gruhn said in a statement.

The company already provides trading technology for Perpetual Markets MTF, a Cyprus-based marketplace licensed under Europe's MiFID II framework that also received authorization under the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation in August.

The firm reported $65.2 million in total assets at the end of April, while posting a $17.6 million net loss during its fiscal year.

It also announced an agreement with Datavault AI earlier this year to support trading infrastructure for planned tokenized commodity offerings involving copper, gold and other physical assets, with more than $300 million in targeted issuance.

How the new trading venue would work

According to the public notice shared with CoinDesk, Perpetuals' U.S. marketplace will be operated by Kephas Corporation, a Delaware-based subsidiary. Trading would take place through permissioned automated market maker (AMM) liquidity pools, initially on Kronos X Public, an Ethereum-compatible layer-2 blockchain developed by the company.

AMMs use smart contracts and liquidity pools to facilitate trades between buyers and sellers instead of traditional exchange order books. Each pool would pair a tokenized U.S. stock with a digital asset, initially expected to be a form of USDC USDC$1.0003, allowing eligible investors to trade shares against the Circle-issued U.S. dollar-pegged stablecoin.

Perpetuals has not set a firm launch date yet. Trading could begin in mid-November at the earliest following the required 30-day period after the public notice, a company spokesperson told CoinDesk, depending on the completion of market-data and compliance arrangements, smart-contract security reviews and other preparations.

The company also plans to publish updated disclosures, including live smart-contract addresses, before trading begins, the spokesperson added.

title: America's growing digital economy requires power grid updates. Who will foot the bill?
summary: Congress must decide how the U.S. can build the infrastructure its booming digital economy requires while protecting the communities that host it.
content:
Oct 14, 2026, 9:51 a.m. EDT

4 min read

The Ratepayer Protection Act recently failed a procedural vote in the U.S. Senate. With 57 senators voting to advance the measure and 43 opposed, it fell short of the 60 votes needed to move forward. This isn't the end of the story for this policy idea. It is the beginning of a trend that will characterize the end of this year and the next Congress: the push to regulate every layer of the digital infrastructure and AI stack.

Championed by Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio) and Reps. Gabe Evans (R-Colo.) and Kathy Castor (D-Fla.), the Ratepayer Protection Act aims to protect households and small businesses from paying for infrastructure needed by large data centers. It would require state utility regulators and certain utilities to consider standards under which computing facilities with peak electricity demand of at least 100 megawatts would cover the full incremental costs of power generation and grid upgrades needed to serve them. States would retain authority to decide whether to adopt those standards.

Rashan Colbert is the Director of U.S. Policy and Digital Energy Council Policy Lead at the Crypto Council for Innovation

AI and digital asset networks run on facilities that need electricity, equipment, land, and grid connections. As those facilities grow, public decisions about their costs and impacts will help determine where and how quickly they can be built. A company's plans for computing capacity depend on whether a utility can deliver power and whether the surrounding community has confidence in the project. At the Crypto Council for Innovation (CCI), we see these questions becoming central to the policy environment for digital assets and the broader digital economy.

Congress is responding to a growing public question about whether households and small businesses will pay for grid upgrades needed by large data centers. The House passed the Ratepayer Protection Act 417–3. Senate debate has centered on whether asking states to consider a cost recovery standard goes far enough. That question will persist, alongside growing pressure to explain how the country can build the infrastructure its digital economy requires while protecting the communities that host it.

Responsible development starts with a fair expectation: large new loads should account for the infrastructure required to serve them, with costs and risks made clear before projects move forward. If a utility builds for a customer's anticipated demand, its agreements should address what happens if that customer reduces operations or leaves. Families need to know how their bills could be affected. Developers also need clear expectations before committing capital.

Earlier this year the president and leaders of many of the biggest technology companies agreed upon that principle through the Ratepayer Protection Pledge. Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Oracle, and xAI committed to covering the costs of new power generation required for their data centers. In July, the White House announced an expansion bringing over 200 additional utilities, data center developers, cooperatives, and states into the effort. Congress must now work through the details of how public policy should give those commitments effect.

The United States must build enough power and infrastructure to meet its increasing needs. Faster development of generation, transmission, storage, and equipment can ease constraints that cost allocation alone cannot solve. Assigning responsibility for a grid upgrade still leaves the work of permitting it, obtaining equipment, and getting it built. Public policy should make that process more predictable while maintaining protections for communities and the environment.

Workable rules must be grounded in operational reality. A proposed campus faces decisions about utility service and local approvals long before its first server begins operating. Policymakers need to understand those dependencies. Utilities, regulators, developers, and computing companies each hold part of that knowledge, and their experience should inform the rules governing new projects. Communities should have opportunities to ask questions while choices about location and infrastructure can still change.

The ratepayer debate is an early example of the choices Congress and states will face across the digital infrastructure stack, from core inputs like energy to critical infrastructure, including data centers, chips, and servers, up to the frontier models they power. Each layer raises distinct questions. A rule about model safety serves a different purpose from a utility tariff, while limits on the infrastructure beneath those models affect the entire stack and many adjacent issues.

We should expect these debates to intensify as lawmakers respond to constituents and leadership begins to develop an agenda for the next Congress. The challenge will be to understand how individual decisions fit together. Energy policy shapes the availability of compute. Decisions about data center development influence where investment flows. The consequences extend to digital assets, AI and other products and services that depend on the same physical foundation.

CCI's Digital Energy Council brings companies across these connected sectors into policy discussions, drawing on their direct experience building and operating the systems that power the digital economy. Our work will focus on expanding U.S. energy capacity and strengthening grid reliability, with attention to the practical path from a proposed facility to one that is operating.

It is a national imperative that the United States builds the capacity the digital economy needs in a responsible manner, making costs transparent and giving communities confidence that growth will serve them too. As a CCI coalition, the Digital Energy Council reflects what CCI has always done: bring together industry leaders, in this case, across digital assets, AI, and energy, to develop and advocate for sensible, substantive, data-driven policies that spur economic growth, protect consumers, and keep national security strong.

title: Kraken parent Payward to become first crypto firm to buy a EU bank as it expands into deposits, lending
summary: Payward agreed to buy Lithuania’s Saldo Bank, which holds $190 million in total assets, securing an EU license for deposits and lending.
content:
Oct 14, 2026, 9:07 a.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • Payward, the parent company of the crypto exchange Kraken, agreed to acquire Lithuania-based Saldo Bank for an undisclosed amount, which would give it a European Union banking license.
  • The deal would allow Payward to offer European customers interest-bearing deposits, loans, card services and euro payments as it expands beyond cryptocurrency trading.
  • The acquisition, which is subject to regulatory approval and expected to close in 2027, would make Payward the first cryptocurrency company to buy a European bank, according to the Financial Times.

Payward, the parent company of crypto exchange Kraken, said it agreed to acquire Lithuania-based Saldo Bank for an undisclosed amount, giving it a European Union (EU) banking license as it expands beyond crypto trading into traditional financial services.

The acquisition will make Payward the first crypto firm to buy a bank in Europe, according to a Financial Times report, as crypto firms increasingly compete with traditional lenders.

Payward did not immediately respond to a CoinDesk request for more details on the amount of the acquisition deal. Saldo Bank had 163.9 million euros ($180 million) in total assets at the end of 2025, up 22.7% from a year earlier, according to The Banks.

Kraken had been seeking a banking license in Lithuania, CoinDesk reported in July. In the U.S., Payward has applied for a national trust bank charter, while its banking arm secured limited access to the Federal Reserve's payment system.

"A regulated EU bank is the piece that lets us serve European clients the way a primary financial institution should: one place to hold assets, move them freely, and put them to work," said Arjun Sethi, Payward's co-CEO.

The deal allows Payward to offer EU customers interest-bearing bank deposits, loans, card services and euro payments.

Saldo Bank is licensed in Lithuania, Finland, Sweden and Germany, and holds a passport to operate in the Netherlands. It offers deposits, consumer and business loans and payment services.

Payward said its banking business has already originated more than $2 billion in loans and holds a Federal Reserve limited-purpose master account and an electronic money institution license in Ireland.

The deal remains subject to regulatory approval and is expected to close in 2027.

title: Bitcoin (BTC) Price Prediction: Slowing Whale Selling Offers Hope as $81.5K ETF Support Holds
summary: Bitcoin (BTC) is consolidating near $83,000–$84,000 as repeated resistance at $84,000 limits recovery, while the $81,500 US spot Bitcoin ETF cost basis remains a critical support level.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

Bitcoin (BTC) is consolidating near $83,000–$84,000 as repeated resistance at $84,000 limits recovery, while the $81,500 US spot Bitcoin ETF cost basis remains a critical support level.

On-chain data indicates that distribution from longer-term holders has slowed, offering some relief to the market. However, weakening bullish momentum and persistent overhead resistance leave the next Bitcoin price move dependent on whether buyers can defend key support and reclaim higher levels.

Bitcoin Price Today: BTC Struggles to Break Above $84K

Bitcoin continues to trade within an $82,500–$86,500 range, but recent price action suggests that buyers are struggling to regain control. According to a technical analysis published by TradingView contributor inchartswetrust, BTC has faced rejection at $84,000 seven times since Sunday, preventing a sustained move toward the upper boundary.

Bitcoin recorded a second false breakdown below $82,500 in 24 hours, with the 4-hour 200 EMA providing strong support and triggering another rebound. Source: inchartswetrust on TradingView

The repeated rejections are significant because $84,000 represents the midpoint of the current trading range. Although the price has recovered after briefly falling below $82,500, those rebounds have failed to generate lasting upward momentum. Similar attempts on October 8 and October 13 lost strength near the same resistance level.

The analyst also identified the four-hour 200-period exponential moving average (EMA) as an important source of support. The indicator has helped reverse two previous breakdown attempts, suggesting that buyers remain active during short-term declines. However, repeated tests of support can leave the market vulnerable if demand weakens.

For the near-term BTC price outlook, reclaiming $84,000 would provide an initial indication that buying pressure is improving. Until that happens, Bitcoin remains exposed to another test of the lower end of its trading range.

Bitcoin ETF Cost Basis at $81.5K Remains a Key Support

On-chain analytics firm Glassnode has identified the US spot Bitcoin ETF investor cost basis near $81,500 as an important market threshold. BTC has rebounded from this level twice in 2026, making it a closely watched reference point for assessing demand from ETF investors.

Bitcoin has rebounded twice from the US spot ETF cost basis near $81,500, establishing support after trading below that level for most of 2026. Source: @glassnode via X

The level also carries historical significance. During the May 2026 rally, Bitcoin’s advance stalled just below the ETF cost basis, highlighting its potential role as both support and resistance depending on market conditions. Its recent ability to hold as support offers some reassurance, although it does not guarantee that buyers will defend it during another decline.

If BTC falls below $81,500 and fails to recover, Glassnode’s True Market Mean near $77,500 becomes the next major on-chain level to watch. This metric provides another reference point for evaluating Bitcoin’s market valuation relative to the aggregate cost basis of active investors.

The chart shows longer-term buyer cost bases still acting as overhead supply, limiting BTC upside while price consolidates above key on-chain averages. Source: Glassnode via X

Meanwhile, Glassnode’s data indicates that a previous rally toward $88,000 encountered resistance near the break-even level for holders who acquired BTC six to 12 months earlier. The subsequent distribution from wallets holding coins for one to two years has slowed considerably.

The easing of this selling pressure could reduce one source of supply in the market. Nevertheless, longer-term holders’ cost bases remain potential overhead resistance, meaning Bitcoin may need stronger demand to sustain a recovery.

BTC Price Prediction: Can Bitcoin Reclaim $88K?

Technical analyst AliCharts has identified an ascending parallel channel on BTC’s four-hour chart. Under this structure, the recent rebound from the lower boundary creates a potential path toward $88,000 near the channel’s midpoint, followed by $93,000 if upward momentum continues toward the upper boundary.

Bitcoin has bounced from its 4-hour ascending channel support, targeting $88,000 mid-channel and potentially $93,000 at the upper boundary. Source: Ali Martinez via X

These levels represent technical scenarios rather than confirmed price targets. BTC would first need to establish stronger support and overcome the repeated resistance around $84,000 before a sustained advance becomes more convincing.

The immediate bullish scenario depends on BTC holding $82,500. If buyers defend this level and push the price above $84,000, Bitcoin could move toward the upper end of its current $82,500–$86,500 range. A breakout above $86,500 would strengthen the recovery structure and bring higher resistance levels into focus.

The bearish scenario begins with a decisive break below $82,500. In that case, $80,000 would become the next major level to monitor. This price area previously acted as resistance, making it a potentially important test for buyers attempting to prevent a deeper correction.

A sustained move below $80,000 could expose the $76,000–$80,000 trading range. Bitcoin’s ability to establish or recover support around these levels would help determine whether the decline represents a temporary setback or a broader deterioration in market structure.

Looking Ahead: Whale Selling and Market Supply Remain in Focus

Slowing distribution from older Bitcoin holdings provides a constructive development, but it should not be interpreted as definitive evidence that large holders have resumed accumulating BTC. A reduction in selling activity can ease supply pressure without necessarily generating enough demand to drive prices higher.

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The ETF cost basis also offers a useful measure of investor positioning. When BTC trades above this level, ETF investors who acquired exposure near the average cost may remain in a more favorable position. A sustained decline below it could weaken sentiment and increase attention on lower support levels.

Bitcoin’s longer-term recovery will depend on several factors, including spot demand, ETF-related flows, the behavior of long-term holders, and its ability to overcome established resistance. The supplied market data identifies $81,500 as a key support reference, while $84,000 remains the immediate hurdle for a stronger short-term recovery.

For now, the Bitcoin price prediction remains conditional. Holding $82,500 and reclaiming $84,000 would improve the technical outlook, while a breakdown could bring $80,000 and potentially $77,500 into focus. Slower whale selling offers some relief, but buyers still need to demonstrate that demand can sustain a move beyond the current range.

title: TOKEN2049 Takeaways: Stablecoins, Asset Tokenization, and AI Payments
summary:
Every crypto conference brings a wave of new partnerships, products, and concepts. After scrolling through the latest updates, your bookmarks may be full, but the takeaways may not be as
The post TOKEN2049 Takeaways: Stablecoins, Asset Tokenization, and AI Payments  appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Every crypto conference brings a wave of new partnerships, products, and concepts. After scrolling through the latest updates, your bookmarks may be full, but the takeaways may not be as clear. The recently concluded TOKEN2049 also raised plenty of topics worth exploring. At moments like these, opening Catcrs and starting with familiar market data can help you identify areas worth following over the long term, drawing on industry news and market information. Making it a regular starting point for your daily market monitoring can also help connect scattered information and build a consistent approach to tracking developments.

So, which themes from TOKEN2049 this year deserve continued attention?

The TOKEN2049 Week this year featured extensive discussions on payments and treasury management, asset tokenization, AI payments, and on-chain finance. Three themes in particular warrant closer monitoring: stablecoins, asset tokenization, and AI payments.

  • Stablecoins: Payment Settlement and Real-World Adoption 
  • Asset Tokenization: Accessibility, Liquidity, and Redemption 
  • AI Payments: Automation, Authorization, and User Control 
  • How to Evaluate Progress Across These Trends 
  • Key Takeaways

Stablecoins: Payment Settlement and Real-World Adoption 

Start with stablecoins. Fast transfers are one of their most recognizable features. For recipients, however, what matters more is how easily they can use the funds. Receiving funds on-chain is only the first step. The amount they actually receive after conversion and the time it takes for the money to reach their bank account will influence whether they choose to accept payments this way again.

Going forward, watch for newly supported regions, merchant integrations, and changes to conversion and withdrawal fees. Whether newly announced partnerships can reduce waiting times and lower costs is a development worth tracking.

Asset Tokenization: Accessibility, Liquidity, and Redemption 

Next, consider asset tokenization. Bringing bonds, funds, and gold on-chain opens up new possibilities. When researching these products, start by checking whether they are available, who is eligible to participate, where returns come from, and what conditions must be met to exit.

Importantly, the ability to transfer an asset on-chain does not mean it can always be sold easily. Beyond issuance size, actual trading activity, bid-ask spreads, and redemption arrangements also deserve attention.

Using Catcrs with these questions in mind gives daily market monitoring a clearer focus. After identifying an asset of interest, review the underlying business, relevant announcements, and token mechanics, then return to the market data to observe how the market responds.

AI Payments: Automation, Authorization, and User Control 

Another area worth watching is AI payments. When AI moves beyond offering advice to taking action on the user behalf, permission management becomes critical. Look at which products are already available, which tasks AI can complete independently, and how key processes such as payments, identity verification, and settlement are designed.

For example, when AI makes a payment on the user behalf, the way spending limits are set, whether recipients require confirmation, whether transaction records can be accessed, and whether authorization can be revoked at any time will all shape the user experience. More than an impressive demonstration, the ability to understand the process and retain control will determine whether a product can become a genuine part of everyday life.

How to Evaluate Progress Across These Trends 

Stablecoins, asset tokenization, and AI payments address the movement of funds, asset issuance and trading, and intelligent task execution, respectively. Each theme has a different focus, but all require market performance to be assessed alongside actual business progress. Choose one or two projects under each theme, record their current progress, plans yet to be delivered, and a date for your next review. A few weeks later, check whether the products have become available, whether the businesses have gained new users, and whether earlier questions have been answered. This allows research to build over time without having to chase new terminology every day.

Key Takeaways

For those who want to deepen their understanding of digital assets without letting the flood of news disrupt their routine, Catcrs can serve as a starting point for daily market monitoring. Begin with market data, add project information and business updates, then return to the market to test your assessments. This gives every browsing session a clear focus and leaves useful leads for the next round of research.

title: FBI Arrests OpenAI Employee as Anthropic Warns of Self-Replicating AI Spreading to Smart Devices
summary: The FBI has arrested an OpenAI employee accused of planting a concealed recording device in the company's San Francisco office, while Anthropic has warned that advances in artificial intelligence could enable self-replicating AI systems to spread across connected devices.
content:
Skip to content

The FBI has arrested an OpenAI employee accused of planting a concealed recording device in the company's San Francisco office, while Anthropic has warned that advances in artificial intelligence could enable self-replicating AI systems to spread across connected devices.

The OpenAI incident and Anthropic’s warning highlight separate security challenges facing the AI industry, from protecting confidential corporate information to preventing future cyber threats.

The two cases are unrelated in the available reporting. However, both underline the growing importance of security as artificial intelligence becomes more capable and increasingly integrated into business operations and consumer hardware.

FBI Arrests OpenAI Employee in Recording Device Case

Federal authorities arrested Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi national who worked as an engineer at OpenAI, on October 9, 2026. The U.S. Department of Justice announced the case on October 13, stating that Alfozan had been charged with using or attempting to use an electronic device to intercept oral communications.

The thumb-sized device was concealed in toilet paper and plugged into a TV USB port around September 28, 2025. Source: CBS News via X

According to the criminal complaint, OpenAI’s security personnel discovered a concealed audio recording device on September 30 inside an executive conference room at the company’s San Francisco offices. Investigators believe the device had been installed around September 28. It was connected to a USB port on the back of a television and concealed with a small piece of toilet paper.

The conference room was regularly used for discussions involving confidential technical research, product development, commercial plans, and strategic decisions. The FBI said these meetings could also cover government engagements, business relationships, and other nonpublic information about OpenAI’s operations.

OpenAI contacted federal investigators after discovering the device. The company reportedly found that it had encryption and audio-monitoring capabilities, along with a mechanism for transferring data intended to avoid detection.

Investigators also examined activity allegedly associated with Alfozan before the device was discovered. Between September 24 and September 30, a chatbot account associated with his spouse was used to submit prompts about constructing, installing, testing, and encrypting an audio-recording device, according to the Justice Department. The complaint also alleges that a productivity tool was used to seek information about office locations, meeting rooms, calendars and meetings involving company leadership.

Authorities further allege that Alfozan returned to the conference room on October 5 and appeared to check behind the television where the device had been placed. OpenAI security personnel also discovered another similar recording device inside an unattended bag reportedly left in a different room at the office.

OpenAI restricted Alfozan’s access to its systems and facilities and later terminated his employment while cooperating with the investigation. The company said it had not found evidence that he improperly accessed or extracted model weights, source code, or customer data.

“At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data,” OpenAI said in a statement published on X.

The investigation remains ongoing. Alfozan is in federal custody and is scheduled to appear for a detention hearing on October 19. If convicted, he faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison, a fine of up to $250,000, and three years of supervised release. These are potential penalties, not a sentence, and the allegations have not been proven in court.

Timeline of alleged events, as disclosed by the FBI and OpenAI

  • September 24–30: A chatbot account associated with Alfozan’s spouse allegedly submitted prompts related to building and operating an audio-recording device.
  • September 28: Investigators believe the recording device was installed in OpenAI’s executive conference room.
  • September 30: OpenAI personnel discovered the device and contacted the FBI.
  • October 5: Alfozan allegedly returned to check the device’s location. A second similar device was reportedly found in a bag left elsewhere in the office.
  • October 9: The FBI arrested Alfozan, and OpenAI terminated his employment.
  • October 13: Federal authorities publicly announced the arrest and charges.
  • October 19: Alfozan is scheduled for a detention hearing.

Anthropic Warns Self-Replicating AI Could Spread to Smart Devices

In a separate development, Anthropic has warned that relatively small AI models could soon become capable of replicating themselves across vulnerable internet-connected devices. Such systems could potentially use compromised hardware to run AI workloads, creating distributed networks that do not depend entirely on centralized data centers.

The warning highlights that AI worms could spread slowly but remain hard to eliminate because of their decentralized nature and ability to adapt to unfamiliar hardware. Source: ABC News via X

In a research report published on October 12, Anthropic researchers described experiments testing whether AI models could identify unfamiliar hardware, configure software to run a model, and keep replicating across connected machines.

“Our experiments suggest that small AI models may be months away from being capable enough to self-replicate on commercial internet-of-things (IoT) devices, like smart ovens and off-brand Android TV boxes,” the researchers wrote.

The company warned that a self-replicating system could be difficult to shut down if it spread across many devices without a single central control point. However, Anthropic presented this as an emerging risk rather than evidence of an active, widespread threat affecting consumer devices.

Replication Experiment

Anthropic tested several AI models, including Qwen3.5-9B, Gemma4-26B-A4B, Llama3.1-8B, GLM-5.2, and Opus 4.8. The researchers evaluated how well these models could handle different parts of the process, including configuring inference software on unfamiliar hardware and coordinating actions across a network.

Anthropic warns that small AI models could enable self-replicating AI worms by late 2026, spreading slowly but proving difficult to eliminate. Source: @livemint via X

In one experiment, the team distributed Google’s Gemma4-26B-A4B model across 15 inexpensive, off-brand Android TV boxes. The setup demonstrated that consumer hardware with limited computing resources could work together to run an AI model. It did not, by itself, demonstrate a fully autonomous AI worm spreading between real-world devices.

Anthropic also tested replication in a controlled network of eight emulated Android devices hosted on Google Cloud infrastructure. In that environment, GLM-5.2 successfully completed the end-to-end process in four out of five trials, reaching all eight nodes. The experiment used an unauthenticated Android Debug Bridge (ADB) port, making the test environment significantly less secure than properly configured devices.

The researchers acknowledged that the results did not establish that a self-replicating AI worm could reliably compromise commercial smart devices under normal security conditions. Their experiments instead examined whether current models could coordinate the technical steps necessary for replication when access barriers were simplified.

Anthropic estimated that models with 30 billion parameters or fewer could reach the required capability level by the end of 2026 if their performance continued improving at its historical rate. The researchers also noted that the process could be slow on the hardware they examined, potentially giving defenders time to identify unusual activity before a network spread significantly.

Potential Cybersecurity Implications

A successful self-replicating AI system could, in principle, turn vulnerable smart TVs, household appliances, cameras, and other internet-connected devices into a distributed computing network. Rather than relying exclusively on conventional data-center infrastructure, an operator could potentially use compromised devices to run AI workloads or support other malicious activity.

The risk is particularly relevant to internet-of-things (IoT) devices with weak authentication, outdated software, or limited security protections. A model capable of adapting to unfamiliar hardware could make some attacks more flexible, although it would still need a way to access and execute software on target devices.

Anthropic proposed several defensive measures, including monitoring large transfers of AI model files, detecting unusual traffic between devices, using honeypots to inspect suspicious activity, and isolating compromised systems. Improving default IoT security settings could also reduce the number of devices exposed to potential attacks.

For device owners and organizations, the findings reinforce the importance of updating firmware, changing default passwords, restricting unnecessary remote access, and ensuring that administrative interfaces are not exposed without authentication.

The warning does not establish that self-replicating AI worms are already spreading through ordinary smart-home devices. Instead, it identifies a technical capability that researchers believe could become more practical as AI models improve.

Taken together, the OpenAI investigation and Anthropic’s research illustrate distinct sides of the evolving AI security landscape. The recording-device case concerns alleged attempts to obtain confidential information within an AI company, while Anthropic’s experiments explore how increasingly capable models might create new challenges for network defense. Both developments place greater emphasis on access controls, monitoring, and security measures that can keep pace with advancing technology.

title: Flow Crypto – The New Exchange for Kiwis
summary: Eli Hylands is the founder of Flow Crypto, a New Zealand on and off ramp that launched about a month before this recording. He has been involved in crypto for roughly ten years, and before Flow he worked as a software developer and business analyst at IAG. He built the platform largely by himself ov...
content:
Skip to content

Eli Hylands is the founder of Flow Crypto, a New Zealand on and off ramp that launched about a month before this recording. He has been involved in crypto for roughly ten years, and before Flow he worked as a software developer and business analyst at IAG. He built the platform largely by himself over about a year, alongside his day job, after seeing a gap open in the local market.

The link will open a new window. Click the menu and down arrow to download the file.

Why you should listen

When Swyftx acquired Easy Crypto in 2025 and began moving its New Zealand customers across, the country’s best-known retail exchange effectively left the market. Hylands saw the gap. Flow Crypto is his answer: a Kiwi-owned, non-custodial service where customers send New Zealand dollars from their bank account and receive crypto directly in their own wallet, with selling running the other way. It charges a flat 0.79 percent fee, supports up to 50 assets, and is registered on the Financial Service Providers Register. Hylands says the software was the easy part. Securing a bank account took about six months, and the hardest work was compliance: meeting reporting obligations to the Department of Internal Affairs while not asking customers for so much information that signing up becomes a chore. His customers, he says, skew toward altcoins rather than Bitcoin, and span all ages, which surprised him.

title: Kraken Parent Payward Wins Full Dubai License, Plans UAE Launch
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Kraken Parent Payward Wins Full Dubai License, Plans UAE Launch
Kraken currently has more than 100 licenses and registrations worldwide. 
This post Kraken Parent Payward Wins Full Dubai License, Plans UAE Launch first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di Salvo.
content:
Crypto exchange Kraken’s parent company Payward has said it has plans to launch in the United Arab Emirates. 

After receiving full market approval from Dubai’s Virtual Asset Regulatory Authority, Payward said Tuesday that Payward can now operate as a regulated virtual asset service provider serving retail, professional and institutional investors. 

It follows a preliminary approval in May that allowed the company to complete its operational set-up ahead of onboarding clients.

At launch, Kraken clients in the UAE will be able to trade spot and margin with dirham-denominated pairs and fund and withdraw directly in dirhams. 

They’ll also have access to on-chain staking, xStocks tokenized equities and Krak for crypto transfers, while institutional clients gain OTC spot trading and Kraken Prime. Crypto derivatives and new yield products are expected later in 2026 and into 2027, subject to regulatory approval.

Payward holds more than 100 licenses and registrations worldwide, spanning Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.

The expansion comes as the company increasingly makes a number of deals. In September, Bloomberg reported that Nasdaq Inc. was investing $100 million in Payward in a deal valuing the company at $21 billion. Kraken will distribute Nasdaq’s tokenized stocks on its own platform, according to the report.

Payward and SoFi Technologies also recently announced a deal to route SoFi customers’ crypto orders through Kraken Prime, Kraken’s prime brokerage arm launched in 2025, and to list SoFi’s stablecoin on the exchange.

Kraken, like other crypto exchanges, is pushing into the traditional finance world, allowing users to trade stocks, bonds and other assets. The company has sold its app as a “primary account for everything.”

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Bybit Expands Beyond Crypto as CEO Outlines Next Phase of Financial Platform
summary: Dubai, United Arab Emirates, 13th October 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Dubai, United Arab Emirates, 13th October 2026, Chainwire

Dubai, United Arab Emirates, October 13th, 2026, Chainwire

Bybit Co-founder and CEO Ben Zhou has outlined the latest stage of the company’s expansion from a crypto exchange into The New Financial Platform, highlighting new products and collaborations across traditional and digital markets. 

The updates were presented during Bybit’s latest biannual “Keynote with Ben” session titled “Make Your Move”, where Ben discussed the convergence of financial markets and the company’s approach to building for that shift. Held outside the usual studio format, in a gathering with a live audience, the keynote brought Ben together with selected guests to discuss changes in the financial landscape, new technologies and the products shaping Bybit’s next phase.

Four Years of TradFi Expansion, With Stocks Now Live and mStocks Ahead

Four years after entering traditional finance with contracts for difference (CFDs) in 2022, Bybit has established itself as the largest crypto CFD platform, with trading volume reaching as much as $100 billion at its peak. On Oct. 12, the company expanded further into traditional markets with the launch of stock trading for eligible users, providing access to more than 1,000 U.S. stocks and ETFs. Users can trade using USDC, with fractional shares and 24/5 access covering U.S. pre-market, regular and after-hours sessions.

Bybit is also developing mStocks in collaboration with Mantle, with a targeted launch in November. The tokenized stock product is designed to be backed 1:1 by real stocks, with plans to support round-the-clock conversion between eligible stocks and mStocks on Bybit, as well as decentralized exchange trading through automated market maker (AMM) liquidity pools on Mantle. Converted mStocks are also expected to be transferable into Bybit’s Unified Trading Account (UTA) for use as trading collateral, subject to applicable terms and conditions.

Bybit launched IPO Express in June, giving eligible users access to selected IPO opportunities at the offering price through tokenized representations of the underlying securities. The service launched with SpaceX and is designed to extend Bybit’s access beyond secondary-market trading into selected primary-market opportunities.

The latest developments build on Bybit’s expansion into perpetuals, pre-market products, foreign exchange and options. Its TradFi offering now spans more than 600 products across equities, ETFs, indices, commodities and FX. TradFi perpetuals have recorded more than $180 billion in trading volume, while recent additions include Forex Perps and Perp Options, an industry-first options product built on TradFi perpetuals.

Bybit is continuing to develop new perpetual products linked to AI computing and commodities, extending its range of instruments beyond conventional crypto markets.

Extending the Platform into Payments

Beyond trading and investing, Bybit has expanded its payments infrastructure to help customers move funds with greater flexibility. Bybit Pay and Bybit Card support crypto and fiat transfers, merchant payments and everyday spending. The service now connects users with more than 5,000 merchants across 15+ countries and supports transfers to bank accounts and e-wallets, alongside QR payments and other payment services. Bybit has issued more than 4 million Bybit Cards, extending the platform’s use beyond financial markets into payments and spending.

Security and Regulatory Infrastructure

The expansion has been accompanied by investment in security, compliance and technology infrastructure.

In the first half of 2026, Bybit said it intercepted more than 30,000 suspicious withdrawal requests, protecting users from more than $700 million in potential losses.

Bybit also secured five new licenses and regulatory approvals across European Union, the Cayman Islands, Indonesia, South Africa and El Salvador during 2026. These regulatory developments support the company’s efforts to expand its presence across different markets, subject to local requirements.

The company launched Bybit AI in September as a conversational assistant across trading, account management and customer support, with further development planned around the platform’s wider financial services.

“Bybit is all about giving you the speed and scale you need when you Make Your Move. We have brought trading, investing, payments and AI together, and we are continuing to add more markets and more ways to use them. We built the platform. Now it is about giving people the financial freedom to make their own move,” said Ben Zhou, Co-founder and CEO of Bybit.

Building Beyond the Exchange

Four years after entering TradFi, Bybit now combines crypto markets with stocks and ETFs, derivatives, commodities, FX, selected pre-IPO access, payments and AI-powered services. The company’s focus is increasingly on bringing these capabilities together within a single platform while continuing to expand market access, product depth and the infrastructure supporting them.

For Bybit, the development of The New Financial Platform represents the next stage of its growth beyond crypto and into a broader role across global financial markets.

Watch the full keynote here: https://www.bybit.com/en/press/live/keynote-with-ben-h2-2026

#Bybit / #NewFinancialPlatform

title: Meet A7 International, an Innovative Global Platform Designed to Reinvent the International Payments Market
summary: Moscow, Russia, 13th October 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Moscow, Russia, 13th October 2026, Chainwire

Moscow, Russia, October 13th, 2026, Chainwire

A7 International enables businesses and individuals to pay invoices with digital assets, while recipients receive a regular bank transfer, reflecting A7’s international positioning and expanding the geography of settlements available to foreign clients.

In two years of operation, A7 has become one of the key players in the international settlements market. Founded in 2024 to serve the foreign economic activity of Russian businesses, it currently serves around 15,000 companies, processing 10+ trillion roubles in 2025 alone. The services A7 offered domestically sparked interest among businesses from other countries, prompting the company to come up with a new product for foreign clients.

The launch of A7 International marks a new stage in A7’s journey. In response to requests from foreign entrepreneurs, the company is expanding its positioning and creating an export offering for businesses in various countries. It is a remote service compliant with local legislation on digital assets and available only in those jurisdictions where cryptocurrency circulation is permitted.

“We are presenting not just a new product in the lineup, but a new image of A7. We have adapted our service so that it can be used remotely from anywhere in the world. This is precisely the key demand of market participants today. They want to be able to transfer money around the world in a few clicks in the shortest possible time – directly from your smartphone, without lengthy paperwork, hidden fees, or unjustified holds on funds. And we are packaging this demand into a convenient and competitive form,” said Chairman of Bank PSB Petr Fradkov.

The mechanics of the service are simple: the client transfers USDT, and A7 arranges a bank transfer via SWIFT using the counterparty details specified in the invoice. The recipient does not need to accept cryptocurrency or open a crypto wallet: the funds arrive in their bank account.

To submit an application, you need to register in your personal account on the website a7.biz. Individuals undergo identity verification (KYC), and companies undergo corporate data verification (KYB). Then the client uploads the invoice and the necessary documents. The built-in algorithm automatically recognizes the invoice data and helps fill out the application.

“The system operates as follows. AI analyzes the sender and beneficiary, jurisdictions, and key risk factors of the transaction. Based on the verification results, a risk profile of the payment is formed and the available options for processing it are determined. The system compares compliance requirements with the capabilities of the existing payment infrastructure. After that, it recommends the optimal payment route taking into account its cost, speed, reliability, and applicable restrictions. Routing dynamically adapts to changes in conditions and the availability of payment channels. Data accumulated over the years makes it possible to continuously improve the quality of decisions made by the system,” noted A7 CEO Ilan Shor.

At launch, A7 International accepts USDT on the TRON network. Bank transfers are available in US dollars, euros, Chinese yuan, and UAE dirhams. Other currencies are available by prior agreement. The commission is 0.3% for both businesses and individuals. After uploading the invoice, the client sees the final cost of the payment, including commission, in advance.

Payment execution time is from one business day. After the operation is completed, the client receives a SWIFT message or another confirming document. For currency and customs control, the service also provides closing documents.

The presentation of the service took place on a symbolic date and time — October 13 at 13:13.

Video of the official presentation and Customer journey here.

About A7

A7 is a global financial technology company specializing in international payments and settlement solutions for international trade. It was established in 2024 with the involvement of PSB Bank.

A7 is developing an independent global payment infrastructure across more than 100 countries, combining global financial expertise, advanced technology and regulatory compliance. The company’s products include international payments, digital financial assets and promissory notes.

A7 Group works with 15,000 clients, with around 2,000 transactions processed through the system every day. In 2025, approximately 19% of Russian companies’ cross-border trade settlements were processed through A7. In October 2025, A7 received an AA(RU) credit rating with a Stable outlook from ACRA.
